13: # Web Elements and Attributes
14: 
15: This file keeps the detailed HTML element and attribute mechanics. The baseline web markup rules remain in [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW AND OVERLAYS
20: 
21: ### EA1. Modal and non-modal dialog APIs
22: 
23: - **Rule:** Call `showModal()` for a modal `<dialog>`, and call `show()` only when the page must stay interactive. Treat `closedby` as an enhancement, feature-detect it and keep Escape plus an explicit close button available.
24: - **Why:** `showModal()` places the dialog in the top layer, creates a `::backdrop`, moves focus into the dialog and keeps sequential focus inside it. Escape dispatches a cancel request that closes the dialog unless the handler prevents it. `show()` does not make the rest of the page inert or establish modal focus behavior.
25: - **When not to:** Use `show()` for a non-modal prompt that leaves the surrounding page usable.
26: - **Pitfall:** Setting `aria-modal="true"` after calling `show()` does not create modal focus behavior.
27: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `dialog`). Chrome 37 / Firefox 98 / Safari 15.4. Baseline limited availability (web-features `dialog-closedby`). Chrome 134 / Firefox 141 / Safari unsupported.
28: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog
29: 
30: ### EA2. Popover states and invokers
31: 
32: - **Rule:** Use `popover="auto"` for light-dismiss behavior or `popover="manual"` when the project owns dismissal, and connect declarative controls with `popovertarget`. Feature-detect the `source` option and `popover="hint"`; keep an explicit anchor and an auto or manual popover path.
33: - **Why:** An auto popover joins the browser's auto popover stack and closes on light dismissal. A manual popover stays open until code or an explicit control closes it. `showPopover({ source })` can set the invoker as the implicit anchor for CSS anchor positioning.
34: - **When not to:** Use a dialog when the surface needs modal focus behavior or blocks the page behind it.
35: - **Pitfall:** `popover="hint"` can layer hint popovers without replacing an open auto popover, but its support is not uniform across the declared browsers.
36: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2025-01-27 (web-features `popover`). Chrome 116 / Firefox 125 / Safari 17. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome 137 / Firefox 144 / Safari 26. Baseline limited availability (web-features `popover-hint`). Chrome 151 / Firefox 153 / Safari unsupported.
37: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API/Using
38: 
39: ---
40: 
41: ## 2. DISCLOSURE AND INERT CONTENT
42: 
43: ### EA3. Exclusive details and find-in-page content
44: 
45: - **Rule:** Use `<summary>` as the first child of `<details>`, and share a `name` only when one-open-at-a-time disclosure is intended.
46: - **Why:** The summary is the disclosure's activation control, and details elements with the same name form an exclusive group. When `hidden="until-found"` is supported, listen for `beforematch` to reveal a containing disclosure before the browser scrolls to a match. Keep an explicit reveal control as the baseline.
47: - **When not to:** Leave details elements unnamed when readers need to compare several open sections.
48: - **Pitfall:** Removing or collapsing a hidden ancestor after `beforematch` can hide the found text again before the browser scrolls to it. The `beforematch` compatibility row is unconfirmed, so keep an explicit reveal control.
49: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-09-03 (web-features `details-name`). Chrome 120 / Firefox 130 / Safari 17.2. Baseline limited availability (web-features `hidden-until-found`). Chrome 102 / Firefox 148 / Safari unsupported.
50: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/hidden
51: 
52: ### EA4. Inert background boundary
53: 
54: - **Rule:** Set `inert` only on the background subtree that must stop receiving focus and interaction while a custom modal is open.
55: - **Why:** The attribute makes descendant controls unavailable for focus and user interaction until it is removed. See [A6](web-accessibility-patterns.md#a6-inert-background) for the modal decision about when the background needs this boundary.
56: - **When not to:** Do not inert the background for a non-modal surface that leaves page controls usable.
57: - **Pitfall:** If the overlay sits inside the subtree marked `inert`, its own controls become unavailable too.
58: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-10-11 (web-features `inert`). Chrome 102 / Firefox 112 / Safari 15.5.
59: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/inert
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: ## 3. INPUT AND SUBMISSION ATTRIBUTES
64: 
65: ### EA5. Keyboard hints and autocomplete tokens
66: 
67: - **Rule:** Set `inputmode` for the expected data, `enterkeyhint` for the next action and `autocomplete` for the field's actual purpose.
68: - **Why:** Keyboard hints influence the virtual keyboard without validating the value. Autocomplete tokens let browsers and credential managers identify fields by meaning. Use `username`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `one-time-code` and `webauthn` for sign-in, password, verification and passkey flows. Use `cc-name`, `cc-given-name`, `cc-additional-name`, `cc-family-name`, `cc-number`, `cc-exp`, `cc-exp-month`, `cc-exp-year`, `cc-csc` and `cc-type` for payment-card fields. Use `tel-national` for a national phone number and `address-line1`, `address-line2` or `address-line3` for separate address lines.
69: - **When not to:** Omit a keyboard hint when the default keyboard already fits the input and its next action.
70: - **Pitfall:** Using `autocomplete="off"` on sign-in or payment fields can block useful credential or payment autofill.
71: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-06-07 (web-features `inputmode`). Chrome 66 / Firefox 95 / Safari 12.1. Baseline widely available since 2024-05-02 (web-features `enterkeyhint`). Chrome 77 / Firefox 94 / Safari 13.1. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome Unknown / Firefox Unknown / Safari Unknown.
72: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/autocomplete
73: 
74: ### EA6. Form owner and submitter overrides
75: 
76: - **Rule:** Set `form` when a control belongs to a form elsewhere in the document, and read the activated submitter's override when handling submission.
77: - **Why:** A control's `form` attribute associates it with a form by ID. The submitter's `formaction` overrides the owning form's `action` for that submission.
78: - **When not to:** Omit these attributes when every control is inside its form and all submitters share one destination.
79: - **Pitfall:** Reading only `form.action` ignores a submit button's `formaction` destination.
80: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
81: - **See also:** https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#form-submission-algorithm
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## 4. LINKS, EMBEDS AND RESOURCE HINTS
86: 
87: ### EA7. Link isolation and request credentials
88: 
89: - **Rule:** Add `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to a new-tab link when it must not control the opener, and choose `referrerpolicy` and `crossorigin` for the request's privacy and CORS needs. Common referrer policy values include `no-referrer`, `origin` and `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.
90: - **Why:** `noopener` removes the new browsing context's access to its opener. `noreferrer` also suppresses the referrer. `crossorigin` selects how a media request uses CORS credentials.
91: - **When not to:** Keep the referrer when the destination depends on it for a documented analytics or return-flow contract.
92: - **Pitfall:** Adding `noreferrer` without checking the destination can remove attribution that the product expects.
93: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-03-20 (web-features `referrer-policy`). Chrome 85 / Firefox 87 / Safari 15. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome 13 / Firefox 8 / Safari 6.
94: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/noopener
95: 
96: ### EA8. Image loading and decoding hints
97: 
98: - **Rule:** Treat `fetchpriority` as a scheduler hint, `loading` as a fetch timing hint and `decoding` as a display scheduling hint.
99: - **Why:** These attributes affect different stages of image work and do not replace reserved dimensions or correct source selection.
100: - **When not to:** Leave default priority on ordinary images that are neither urgent nor a known loading bottleneck.
101: - **Pitfall:** Lazy-loading an image that becomes the largest contentful paint delays the page's primary visual response. See the [LCP resource rule](web-performance-and-loading.md#p1-largest-contentful-paint-resource).
102: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-10-29 (web-features `fetch-priority`). Chrome 103 / Firefox 132 / Safari 17.2. Baseline widely available since 2026-06-19 (web-features `loading-lazy`). Chrome 77 / Firefox 121 / Safari 16.4. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome 65 / Firefox 63 / Safari 11.1.
103: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/img
104: 
105: ### EA9. Document language and translation hints
106: 
107: - **Rule:** Keep `lang`, `dir` and `translate` aligned with the language and direction of the content.
108: - **Why:** These attributes expose language and text direction to browser features and assistive technology, while `translate="no"` marks names or code that machine translation should retain. Inline language, bidirectional text and locale formatting details are in [web-internationalization.md](web-internationalization.md#1-overview-and-language-and-direction).
109: - **When not to:** Do not set a local language or direction override when the text follows the surrounding passage.
110: - **Pitfall:** A missing inline language or direction override can make a short foreign phrase render or sound incorrectly inside otherwise correct page metadata.
111: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2018-01-29 (web-features `lang-attr`). Chrome 1 / Firefox 1 / Safari ≤4. Baseline widely available since 2018-01-29 (web-features `dir`). Chrome 1 / Firefox 1 / Safari 3. Baseline widely available since 2025-09-14 (web-features `translate`). Chrome 19 / Firefox 111 / Safari 6.
112: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/lang

50:

52:

61:

140: ### A11. Carousel

150:

164: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
165: - **See also:** https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/
166: 
167: ### A14. Tooltip
168: 
169: - **Rule:** Give supplemental content `role="tooltip"`, associate its trigger through `aria-describedby`, show it on hover and focus and let Escape dismiss it.

172: - **Pitfall:** A tooltip on a disabled control may never appear, and a tooltip cannot provide the control's only name.
173: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
174: - **See also:** https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/

178: ## 6. FORMS AND VALIDATION
179: 
180: ### A15. Angular owns constraint validation
181: 
182: - **Rule:** For forms handled by a framework validation layer, render app feedback and confirm whether the framework disables native browser validation. Keep native constraint attributes so the framework can read them.
183: - **Why:** A framework may add `novalidate` or otherwise replace browser validation bubbles while still using attributes such as `required` and `min` as validator inputs.

185: - **Pitfall:** `setCustomValidity()` does not restore browser validation UI while `novalidate` remains on the form.
186: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
187: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Constraint_validation
188: 
189: ### A16. Error association in Angular Material and hand-written fields
190: 
191: - **Rule:** Inside a component library's form-field wrapper, let the library associate its error and hint messages. In a hand-written field, bind the visible message ID and invalid state to the control.
192: - **Why:** A library may add message IDs to the input's `aria-describedby` list and update its `aria-invalid` state. For a hand-written field, give each message an ID, reference it from the control and set the invalid state when validation fails.

195: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
196: - **See also:** https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/

198: ### A17. Error summary and focus on submit
199: 
200: - **Rule:** After a failed submit, focus the first invalid control or an error summary that links to each invalid control.
201: - **Why:** The summary gives assistive technology users one place to review errors and jump to the affected fields.
202: - **When not to:** A single-field form, such as a search box, can keep focus on its field and show the inline error there.
203: - **Pitfall:** After a submit handler calls `markAllAsTouched()`, focus remains on the submit button unless code moves it. Newly rendered error text is not automatically announced.
204: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
205: - **See also:** https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/
206: 
207: ### A18. Async validator pending state
208: 
209: - **Rule:** Block submission while a form is pending as well as when it is invalid. Expose validation progress with `aria-busy` on the field group or a polite status message.
210: - **Why:** An asynchronous validator can leave a form pending while both its valid and invalid states are false.
211: - **When not to:** A form with no async validators needs only the `invalid` check.
212: - **Pitfall:** A submit check that reads only `form.invalid` can run before async validation finishes. A disabled control leaves the tab order and is excluded from the form's aggregate value.
213: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
214: - **See also:** https://angular.dev/api/forms/AbstractControl

193: - **When not to:** Do not add a duplicate `aria-describedby` ID or invalid-state binding when the component already manages both.
194: - **Pitfall:** A library may show an error when a control is invalid and touched or when the form is submitted. A hand-written component that shows errors only when dirty behaves differently.
195: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
196: - **See also:** https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/
197: 
198: ### A17. Error summary and focus on submit
199: 
200: - **Rule:** After a failed submit, focus the first invalid control or an error summary that links to each invalid control.
201: - **Why:** The summary gives assistive technology users one place to review errors and jump to the affected fields.
202: - **When not to:** A single-field form, such as a search box, can keep focus on its field and show the inline error there.
203: - **Pitfall:** After a submit handler calls `markAllAsTouched()`, focus remains on the submit button unless code moves it. Newly rendered error text is not automatically announced.
204: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
205: - **See also:** https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/
206: 
207: ### A18. Async validator pending state
208: 
209: - **Rule:** Block submission while a form is pending as well as when it is invalid. Expose validation progress with `aria-busy` on the field group or a polite status message.
210: - **Why:** An asynchronous validator can leave a form pending while both its valid and invalid states are false.
211: - **When not to:** A form with no async validators needs only the `invalid` check.
212: - **Pitfall:** A submit check that reads only `form.invalid` can run before async validation finishes. A disabled control leaves the tab order and is excluded from the form's aggregate value.
213: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
214: - **See also:** https://angular.dev/api/forms/AbstractControl

13: # Web Internationalization
14: 
15: This file keeps browser language, direction and locale formatting mechanics. The baseline web markup rules remain in [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW AND LANGUAGE AND DIRECTION
20: 
21: Support summaries use the web-features Baseline classifications and browser-version data.
22: 
23: ### I1. Language tags
24: 
25: - **Rule:** Set a valid BCP 47 `lang` on the document and on inline spans whose language differs from the surrounding text.
26: - **Why:** Browsers and assistive technology use language metadata for pronunciation, hyphenation, spellcheck and language-aware selectors.
27: - **When not to:** Omit a local override when the phrase uses the surrounding language.
28: - **Pitfall:** A correct document language does not identify a foreign-language name or phrase inside an otherwise different-language paragraph.
29: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2018-01-29 (web-features `lang-attr`). Chrome 1 / Firefox 1 / Safari ≤4.
30: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/lang
31: 
32: ### I2. Direction and automatic direction
33: 
34: - **Rule:** Set `dir="rtl"` for a right-to-left document and use `dir="auto"` for user-provided strings with unknown direction.
35: - **Why:** Automatic direction follows the first strong directional character, while an explicit document direction controls the page's base writing direction.
36: - **When not to:** Keep the inherited direction when a string is known to follow the surrounding content.
37: - **Pitfall:** Under `dir="auto"`, an Arabic username that begins with a Latin brand name is treated as left-to-right, because the first strong character decides. Digits are weak and do not decide.
38: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2018-01-29 (web-features `dir`). Chrome 1 / Firefox 1 / Safari 3.
39: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/dir
40: 
41: ### I3. Bidirectional isolation
42: 
43: - **Rule:** Wrap interpolated user text in `<bdi>` or isolate an inline span with `unicode-bidi: isolate`.
44: - **Why:** Isolation keeps the embedded text's directional ordering from affecting adjacent text and punctuation.
45: - **When not to:** Skip an isolate when the embedded text is already in a separate block with its own direction.
46: - **Pitfall:** An RTL name interpolated into an LTR sentence can move the trailing punctuation to the wrong visual side.
47: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `bdi`). Chrome 16 / Firefox 10 / Safari 6.
48: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/bdi
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 2. LAYOUT AND DIRECTIONAL ICONS
53: 
54: ### I4. Logical properties and writing modes
55: 
56: - **Rule:** Use the CSS mapping in [web-layout-and-sizing.md](web-layout-and-sizing.md#5-logical-properties) when dimensions and edges must follow the writing mode.
57: - **Why:** The layout reference owns the physical-to-logical property mechanics and their interaction with writing modes.
58: - **When not to:** Keep physical coordinates for intentionally physical surfaces such as a canvas whose origin is fixed to the left edge.
59: - **Pitfall:** Mixing physical and logical sides in one rule lets declaration order choose the edge in one direction and a different edge in another.
60: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
61: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_logical_properties_and_values
62: 
63: ### I5. Directional icon mirroring
64: 
65: - **Rule:** Mirror arrows and chevrons whose meaning follows inline reading direction, and keep direction-neutral or physical icons unchanged.
66: - **Why:** Directional icons encode forward or backward movement, while a logo, clock, checkmark or media control keeps the same meaning in either writing direction.
67: - **When not to:** Do not mirror an icon whose symbol depicts a fixed physical object or an invariant action.
68: - **Pitfall:** Mirroring a play or checkmark icon reverses a symbol whose meaning does not depend on text direction.
69: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
70: - **See also:** https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-scripts
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## 3. LOCALE FORMATTING
75: 
76: ### I6. Intl formatting and plural categories
77: 
78: - **Rule:** Pass the active locale explicitly to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `NumberFormat`, `PluralRules`, `RelativeTimeFormat`, `ListFormat`, `Collator`, `Segmenter` and `DisplayNames`.
79: - **Why:** An explicit locale keeps formatting aligned with the app language instead of the browser's unrelated default. `PluralRules` exposes locale-specific categories, including six categories in Arabic and few or many categories in Polish.
80: - **When not to:** Use a locale-independent representation when the value is an identifier or machine protocol field rather than reader-facing text.
81: - **Pitfall:** A `count === 1` branch assumes two plural forms and fails for languages with additional categories.
82: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
83: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl
84: 
85: ### I7. Date-only parsing
86: 
87: - **Rule:** Parse date-only values as calendar dates in the intended locale and time zone instead of converting them through UTC timestamps.
88: - **Why:** JavaScript parses an ISO date-only string such as `2026-11-02` at UTC midnight, which can display as the previous local date in a negative offset.
89: - **When not to:** Use a timestamp when the input represents an exact instant rather than a calendar date.
90: - **Pitfall:** Calling `toISOString().slice(0, 10)` on a local date can serialize a different calendar day.
91: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
92: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Date/parse
93: 
94: ---
95: 
96: ## 4. ANGULAR LOCALE WIRING
97: 
98: ### I8. Angular pipes with runtime translations
99: 
100: - **Rule:** In Angular, register locale data for supported locales and provide `LOCALE_ID` from the active locale at the app boundary. Other frameworks should pass the active locale to their formatting services.
101: - **Why:** A language change must also update date, number and currency formatting; changing translated strings alone does not change formatting data.
102: - **When not to:** Keep the default locale when formatted data intentionally remains in that locale.
103: - **Pitfall:** A date-picker locale setting may not change the locale used by other date, number or currency formatters.
104: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
105: - **See also:** https://angular.dev/guide/i18n/format-data-locale
106: 
107: ---
108: 
109: ## 5. TRANSLATION-TOLERANT TEXT
110: 
111: ### I9. Expansion and pseudo-localization
112: 
113: - **Rule:** Test layouts with pseudo-localized text and leave room for German and Dutch strings that can grow by about 30 to 35 percent.
114: - **Why:** Translation changes word length and line breaks, which can push fixed-width controls past their available space.
115: - **When not to:** Use a fixed measure only when the content has a documented hard limit, such as a machine identifier.
116: - **Pitfall:** A button that fits the source language can clip its translated label when its width is fixed.
117: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
118: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Localization/Localization_and_Plurals

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ### When to Create References
37: 
38: **Create a reference file when:**
39: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
40: - Decision trees with multiple branches
41: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
42: - Systematic debugging procedures
43: - Tool integration details
44: - Content exceeds 200 lines
45: 
46: **Keep in SKILL.md when:**
47: - Content under 200 lines
48: - Simple workflows (3-5 steps)
49: - Overview and "When to Use" sections
50: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
55: 
56: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
57: 
58: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
59: 
60: ```markdown
61: ---
62: title: [Title]
63: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
64: trigger_phrases:
65:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
66:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
67:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
68: importance_tier: normal
69: contextType: general
70: version: 1.0.0.0
71: ---
72: 
73: # [Title]
74: 
75: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: \## 1. OVERVIEW
80: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
81: 
82: ```
83: 
84: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
85: 
86: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
87: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
88: 
89: #### GOOD Intro Structure
90: 
91: ```markdown
92: # Git Commit Workflows
93: 
94: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: \## 1. OVERVIEW
99: 
100: ### Purpose
101: Provides systematic workflows for analyzing changes, filtering artifacts, and creating well-structured commits.
102: 
103: ### When to Use
104: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
105: - Filtering generated files from commits
106: - Writing clear commit messages
107: 
108: ### Core Principle
109: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
110: ```
111: 
112: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
113: 
114: ```markdown
115: # Git Commit Workflows
116: 
117: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
118: 
119: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
120: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
121: 
122: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
123: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: \## 1. OVERVIEW
128: 
129: ### Purpose
130: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
131: 
132: ### Core Principle
133: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
134: ```
135: 
136: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
137: 
138: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
139: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
140: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
141: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
142: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
143: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
144: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
145: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
146: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
151: 
152: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
153: 
154: **Core Purpose**:
155: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
156: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
157: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
158: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
159: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
160: 
161: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
162: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
163: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
164: 
165: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
166: 
167: ```
168: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
169:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
170:             ↓
171: Level 2: SKILL.md body
172:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
173:             ↓
174: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
175:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
176: ```
177: 
178: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
179: 
180: ---
181: 
182: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
183: 
184: ### Create Reference File When
185: 
186: **Workflow Complexity**:
187: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
188: - Decision trees with multiple branches
189: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
190: - Systematic debugging procedures
191: 
192: **Technical Depth**:
193: - Root cause analysis required
194: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
195: - Before/after code transformations
196: - Common error patterns and fixes
197: 
198: **Size Threshold**:
199: - Content exceeds 200 lines
200: - Multiple related workflows
201: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
202: 
203: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
204: 
205: **Core Content**:
206: - Overview and "When to Use"
207: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
208: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
209:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
210: - Quick reference
211: 
212: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
213: 
214: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
215: 
216: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
217: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
218: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
219: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
220: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |

622: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
623: 
624: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
625: 
626: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
627: 
628: **Decision Criteria**:
629: 
630: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
631: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
632: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
633: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
634: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
635: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
636: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
637: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
638: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
639: 
640: ### Extraction Pattern
641: 
642: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
643: ```markdown
644: ### [Workflow Name]
645: 
646: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
647: 
648: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
649: 
650: **Quick Overview**:
651: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
652: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
653: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
654: 
655: **Configuration Options:**
656: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
657: - Default values optimized for common use cases
658: ```
659: 
660: ### Benefits of Separation
661: 
662: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
663: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
664: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
665: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
666: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
667: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
668: 
669: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
670: 
671: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
672: \```python
673: def detect_mode(request):
674:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
675:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
676:     return 'interactive', 10
677: \```
678: 
679: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
680: 
681: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
682: \```python
683: from dataclasses import dataclass
684: 
685: @dataclass
686: class ModeConfig:
687:     mode: str
688:     depth_rounds: int
689: 
690: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
691:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
692:     if '$quick' in request:
693:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
694:     elif '$ticket' in request:
695:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
696:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
697: \```
698: 
699: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
700: \```python
701: def test_quick_mode():
702:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
703: \```
704: 
705: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
706:

709: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
710: 
711: ### Purpose
712: 
713: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
714: 
715: **When to use YAML**:
716: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
717: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
718: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
719: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
720: - Validation schemas
721: 
722: ### Standard YAML Structure
723: 
724: ```yaml
725: # [config-name].yaml
726: metadata:
727:   version: "1.0.0"
728:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
729: 
730: config:
731:   threshold_values:
732:     low: 1
733:     medium: 5
734:     high: 10
735:   feature_flags:
736:     enable_feature_x: true
737:   mappings:
738:     $quick: "quick_mode"
739:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
740: ```
741: 
742: ### File Organization
743: 
744: ```
745: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
746: ├── assets/
747: │   ├── workflow-configs/
748: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
749: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
750: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
751: │   ├── mappings/
752: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
753: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
754: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
755: │   └── templates/
756: │       └── [template files]
757: ```
758: 
759: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
760: 
761: ```python
762: import yaml
763: from pathlib import Path
764: 
765: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
766:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
767:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
768:     with open(config_path) as f:
769:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
770: 
771: # Usage
772: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
773: ```
774: 
775: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
776: 
777: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
778: ```markdown
779: | Trigger                    | Action             |
780: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
781: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
782: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
783: ```
784: 
785: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
786: 
787: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
788: ```yaml
789: config:
790:   variant_triggers:
791:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
792:     implicit:
793:       complexity_threshold: 7
794:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
795:   variant_count:
796:     simple: [2, 3]
797:     complex: [5, 10]
798: ```
799: 
800: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
801: ```python
802: import yaml
803: 
804: class VariantDetector:
805:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
806:         with open(config_path) as f:
807:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
808: 
809:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
810:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
811:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
812:             return True
813: 
814:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
815:         if complexity >= threshold:
816:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
817:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
818:         return False
819: ```
820: 
821: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
822:

825: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
826: 
827: ### When to Use Python for Logic
828: 
829: **Use Python scripts when**:
830: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
831: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
832: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
833: - API integration (external services)
834: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
835: 
836: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
837: 
838: **Always include**:
839: - Type hints for parameters and return values
840: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
841: - Dataclasses for structured data
842: 
843: **Example**:
844: ```python
845: from dataclasses import dataclass
846: from pathlib import Path
847: 
848: @dataclass
849: class ValidationResult:
850:     is_valid: bool
851:     errors: list[str]
852: 
853: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
854:     """
855:     Validate configuration file.
856: 
857:     Args:
858:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
859: 
860:     Returns:
861:         ValidationResult with status and errors
862: 
863:     Raises:
864:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
865:     """
866:     if not config_path.exists():
867:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
868:     # Validation logic
869:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
870: ```
871: 
872: ### Unit Testing Requirements
873: 
874: **Every Python script must have tests**:
875: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
876: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
877: - Framework: pytest
878: 
879: **Example**:
880: ```python
881: import pytest
882: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
883: 
884: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
885:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
886:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
887:     result = validate_config(config)
888:     assert result.is_valid
889: 
890: def test_validate_missing_file():
891:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
892:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
893: ```
894: 
895: ### Import and Reference Patterns
896: 
897: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
898: 
899: **Markdown references**:
900: ```markdown
901: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
902: ```
903: 
904: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
905: 
906: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
907: ```markdown
908: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
909: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
910: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
911: ```
912: 
913: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
914: 
915: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
916: ```python
917: from typing import Literal
918: from dataclasses import dataclass
919: 
920: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
921: 
922: @dataclass
923: class WorkflowDecision:
924:     mode: WorkflowMode
925:     depth_rounds: int
926: 
927: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
928:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
929:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
930:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
931:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
932:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
933:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
934: ```
935: 
936: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
937: ```python
938: def test_quick_mode():
939:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
940: 
941: def test_default_mode():
942:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
943: ```
944: 
945: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills

18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ### When to Create References
37: 
38: **Create a reference file when:**
39: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
40: - Decision trees with multiple branches
41: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
42: - Systematic debugging procedures
43: - Tool integration details

46: **Keep in SKILL.md when:**
47: - Content under 200 lines
48: - Simple workflows (3-5 steps)
49: - Overview and "When to Use" sections
50: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
55: 
56: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
57: 
58: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
59: 
60: ```markdown
61: ---
62: title: [Title]
63: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
64: trigger_phrases:
65:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
66:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
67:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
68: importance_tier: normal
69: contextType: general
70: version: 1.0.0.0
71: ---
72: 
73: # [Title]
74: 
75: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: \## 1. OVERVIEW
80: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
81: 
82: ```
83: 
84: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
85: 
86: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
87: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
88: 
89: #### GOOD Intro Structure
90: 
91: ```markdown
92: # Git Commit Workflows
93: 
94: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: \## 1. OVERVIEW
99: 
100: ### Purpose
101: Provides systematic workflows for analyzing changes, filtering artifacts, and creating well-structured commits.
102: 
103: ### When to Use
104: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
105: - Filtering generated files from commits
106: - Writing clear commit messages
107: 
108: ### Core Principle
109: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
110: ```
111: 
112: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
113: 
114: ```markdown

116: 
117: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
118:

125: ---

128: 
129: ### Purpose

131: 
132: ### Core Principle
133: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
134: ```
135: 
136: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
137: 
138: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
139: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |

149: 
150: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
151: 
152: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
153: 
154: **Core Purpose**:
155: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
156: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
157: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
158: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
159: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
160: 
161: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
162: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
163: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
164: 
165: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
166: 
167: ```
168: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
169:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
170:             ↓
171: Level 2: SKILL.md body
172:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
173:             ↓
174: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
175:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
176: ```
177: 
178: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

180: ---

182: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES

186: **Workflow Complexity**:

198: **Size Threshold**:
199: - Content exceeds 200 lines
200: - Multiple related workflows

229: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
230: 
231: ### Core Principle Statements
232: 
233: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
234: 
235: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.

238: ```markdown

240: 
241: ### Core Principle
242:

245: 
246: **Examples from Real Skills**:
247: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
248: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
249: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"

251: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
252: 
253: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
254: 
255: **Format**:
256: ```markdown
257: ### The [Number] Phases
258:

262:

621: 
622: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
623: 
624: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
625: 
626: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
627: 
628: **Decision Criteria**:
629: 
630: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
631: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
632: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
633: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
634: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
635: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
636: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
637: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
638: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
639: 
640: ### Extraction Pattern
641: 
642: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
643: ```markdown
644: ### [Workflow Name]
645: 
646: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
647: 
648: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
649: 
650: **Quick Overview**:
651: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
652: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
653: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
654: 
655: **Configuration Options:**
656: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
657: - Default values optimized for common use cases
658: ```
659: 
660: ### Benefits of Separation
661: 
662: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
663: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
664: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
665: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
666: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
667: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
668: 
669: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
670:

708: 
709: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
710: 
711: ### Purpose
712: 
713: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
714: 
715: **When to use YAML**:
716: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
717: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
718: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
719: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
720: - Validation schemas
721: 
722: ### Standard YAML Structure
723: 
724: ```yaml
725: # [config-name].yaml
726: metadata:
727:   version: "1.0.0"
728:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
729: 
730: config:
731:   threshold_values:
732:     low: 1
733:     medium: 5
734:     high: 10
735:   feature_flags:
736:     enable_feature_x: true
737:   mappings:
738:     $quick: "quick_mode"
739:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
740: ```
741: 
742: ### File Organization
743: 
744: ```
745: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
746: ├── assets/
747: │   ├── workflow-configs/
748: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
749: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
750: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
751: │   ├── mappings/
752: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
753: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
754: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
755: │   └── templates/
756: │       └── [template files]
757: ```
758: 
759: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
760: 
761: ```python
762: import yaml
763: from pathlib import Path
764: 
765: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
766:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
767:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
768:     with open(config_path) as f:
769:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
770: 
771: # Usage
772: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
773: ```
774: 
775: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
776: 
777: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
778: ```markdown
779: | Trigger                    | Action             |
780: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
781: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
782: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
783: ```
784: 
785: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
786: 
787: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
788: ```yaml
789: config:
790:   variant_triggers:
791:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
792:     implicit:
793:       complexity_threshold: 7
794:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
795:   variant_count:
796:     simple: [2, 3]
797:     complex: [5, 10]
798: ```
799: 
800: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
801: ```python
802: import yaml
803: 
804: class VariantDetector:
805:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
806:         with open(config_path) as f:
807:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
808: 
809:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
810:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
811:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
812:             return True
813: 
814:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
815:         if complexity >= threshold:
816:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
817:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
818:         return False
819: ```

821: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

825: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
826: 
827: ### When to Use Python for Logic
828: 
829: **Use Python scripts when**:
830: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
831: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
832: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
833: - API integration (external services)
834: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
835: 
836: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
837: 
838: **Always include**:
839: - Type hints for parameters and return values
840: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
841: - Dataclasses for structured data
842: 
843: **Example**:
844: ```python
845: from dataclasses import dataclass
846: from pathlib import Path
847: 
848: @dataclass
849: class ValidationResult:
850:     is_valid: bool
851:     errors: list[str]
852: 
853: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
854:     """
855:     Validate configuration file.
856: 
857:     Args:
858:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
859: 
860:     Returns:
861:         ValidationResult with status and errors
862: 
863:     Raises:
864:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
865:     """
866:     if not config_path.exists():
867:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")

869:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
870: ```
871: 
872: ### Unit Testing Requirements
873: 
874: **Every Python script must have tests**:
875: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory

879: **Example**:

882: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config

894: 
895: ### Import and Reference Patterns
896: 
897: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
898: 
899: **Markdown references**:
900: ```markdown

949: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
950: 
951: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
952: 
953: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
954: 
955: ```

957: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
958: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
959: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
960: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
961: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
962: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
963: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
964: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
965: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
966: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
967: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
968: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
969: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
970: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
971: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
972: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
973: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
974: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
975: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
976: │       ├── template-name.md

978: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
979:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
980:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
981:     ├── test_config_validator.py
982:     └── __init__.py

984: 
985: ### Directory Purposes
986: 
987: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
988: 
989: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
990: 
991: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
992: 
993: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings

997: ### When to Create Each Directory
998: 
999: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1000: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1001: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1002: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |

212: def should_exclude_path(file_path: str) -> Tuple[bool, Optional[str]]:
213:     """Check if file path should be excluded from validation."""
214:     path_str = str(file_path)
215: 
216:     # Check excluded patterns (auto-generated, dependencies)
217:     for pattern in EXCLUDED_PATH_PATTERNS:
218:         if f'/{pattern}/' in path_str or f'\\{pattern}\\' in path_str:
219:             return True, f"Excluded: matches pattern '{pattern}'"
220: 
221:     # Check third-party patterns
222:     for pattern in THIRD_PARTY_PATTERNS:
223:         if pattern in path_str:
224:             return True, f"Third-party: matches pattern '{pattern}'"
225: 
226:     # Check template patterns (intentionally minimal)
227:     for pattern in TEMPLATE_PATTERNS:
228:         if pattern in path_str:
229:             return True, f"Template: matches pattern '{pattern}' (intentionally minimal)"
230: 
231:     # Check fixture trees: any path segment ending in "fixtures" (mirrors
232:     # package_skill.py's naming exemption), plus known fixture trees that a test
233:     # suite names for a different reason than the literal segment "fixtures".
234:     # A numbered segment such as `001-shared-mode-contracts-and-fixtures` names a
235:     # spec packet or phase, and skipping it would hide that packet's documents.
236:     # The singular "-fixture" folder name (review-output-fixture/) is the same kind
237:     # of tree, so it is matched as a folder segment rather than a file name.
238:     normalized = path_str.replace('\\', '/')
239:     folders = normalized.split('/')[:-1]
240:     if any(part.endswith(('fixtures', 'fixture')) and not SPEC_FOLDER_SEGMENT.match(part)
241:            for part in folders):
242:         return True, "Fixture tree: holds the shapes it exercises"
243:     for pattern in FIXTURE_TREE_PATTERNS:
244:         if pattern in normalized:
245:             return True, f"Fixture tree: matches pattern '{pattern}'"
246: 
247:     if normalized.rsplit('/', 1)[-1] in INSTRUCTION_FILE_NAMES:
248:         return True, "Instruction file: keeps its runtime's own section template"
249: 
250:     if any(normalized.endswith('/' + suffix) for suffix in FORMAT_SPEC_FILES):
251:         return True, "Format spec: its section numbers are the DESIGN.md format's ids"
252: 
253:     return False, None

276: def _detect_document_type_with_source(file_path: str, content: str, rules: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[str, str]:
277:     """Detect document type and whether a path rule ('rule') or the README default ('default') decided it."""
278:     path_lower = str(file_path).lower()
279:     assert_supported_root_path(path_lower)
280:     portable_path = PurePosixPath(path_lower.replace('\\', '/'))
281: 
282:     if any(f'/{name}/' in path_lower or f'\\{name}\\' in path_lower for name in PLAYBOOK_DIR_NAMES):
283:         # A per-feature playbook leaf sits one level below the category root
284:         # (manual-testing-playbook/<category>/<feature>.md). Classify by that structural
285:         # position rather than an ordinal folder-name prefix, so category folders can be
286:         # named by meaning alone. The root index file (whose parent IS the
287:         # manual_testing_playbook dir) is intentionally excluded.
288:         if portable_path.parent.parent.name in PLAYBOOK_DIR_NAMES:
289:             return 'playbook_feature', 'rule'
290:     # Per-feature catalog leaves sit one level below the catalog root
291:     # (feature-catalog/<category>/<feature>.md). These carry the Validation And Tests
292:     # table whose Type taxonomy and placeholder rows the generic readme path misses.
293:     # Classify by structural position rather than an ordinal folder-name prefix; the
294:     # root index file (whose parent IS the feature_catalog dir) stays excluded.
295:     if any(f'/{name}/' in path_lower or f'\\{name}\\' in path_lower for name in CATALOG_DIR_NAMES):
296:         if portable_path.parent.parent.name in CATALOG_DIR_NAMES:
297:             return 'feature_catalog', 'rule'
298:     # A README inside a commands folder uses the .markdown extension so OpenCode does
299:     # not register it as a command, and the commands-folder rule would misread it.
300:     if portable_path.name == 'readme.markdown':
301:         return 'readme', 'rule'
302:     if '/command/' in path_lower or '\\command\\' in path_lower or '/commands/' in path_lower or '\\commands\\' in path_lower:
303:         return 'command', 'rule'
304:     # Changelog files: under .skilled/changelog/, .skilled/skills/*/changelog/,
305:     # or spec-folder nested changelog/ subdirectories. Files match v{VERSION}.md or changelog-*.md
306:     # The folder decides before any word in the name does, so a packet changelog
307:     # about install guides is still a changelog.
308:     if '/changelog/' in path_lower or '\\changelog\\' in path_lower:
309:         return 'changelog', 'rule'
310:     # An install guide is a document a skill owns next to its own SKILL.md, named
311:     # INSTALL-GUIDE.md. Classify it by that filename, the only thing that marks it.
312:     if 'install_guide' in Path(path_lower).stem or 'install-guide' in Path(path_lower).stem:
313:         return 'install_guide', 'rule'
314:     # A repository security policy is named SECURITY.md wherever it sits, the root or
315:     # .github/, and only that exact name marks it. The match is case-sensitive so a
316:     # lowercase security.md reference or playbook leaf keeps its own type.
317:     if Path(str(file_path)).name == 'SECURITY.md':
318:         return 'security_policy', 'rule'
319:     # A skill or mode keeps its machine router in a sibling ROUTER.md, and only that
320:     # exact name marks it. Without this rule a router fell back to README rules.
321:     if Path(str(file_path)).name == 'ROUTER.md':
322:         return 'skill_router', 'rule'
323:     # A companion file sits in a run folder below benchmark/reports/, either directly
324:     # (reports/<run>/) or under a grouping folder (reports/<group>/<run>/).
325:     if (portable_path.name in BENCHMARK_COMPANION_NAMES
326:             and '/benchmark/reports/' in f'/{portable_path.parent.parent.as_posix()}/'):
327:         return 'benchmark_companion', 'rule'
328:     if path_lower.endswith('readme.md'):
329:         return 'readme', 'rule'
330:     if path_lower.endswith('skill.md'):
331:         return 'skill', 'rule'
332:     if '/specs/' in path_lower or '\\specs\\' in path_lower:
333:         return 'spec', 'rule'
334:     if '/agents/' in path_lower or '\\agents\\' in path_lower or '/agent/' in path_lower or '\\agent\\' in path_lower:
335:         return 'agent', 'rule'
336:     if '/references/' in path_lower or '\\references\\' in path_lower:
337:         return 'reference', 'rule'
338:     # A skill scaffold is the template a renderer copies into SKILL.md, so the sections
339:     # it must carry are the ones that file needs, not the asset rule's Overview, which
340:     # no SKILL.md ever has. Name and the assets/ ancestor together mark a template;
341:     # either alone would also catch written documentation.
342:     if 'scaffold' in portable_path.stem and ('/assets/' in path_lower or '\\assets\\' in path_lower):
343:         return 'skill', 'rule'
344:     if '/assets/' in path_lower or '\\assets\\' in path_lower:
345:         return 'asset', 'rule'
346: 
347:     # Default to readme for general markdown
348:     return 'readme', 'default'

375: def extract_section_name_text(text: str) -> str:
376:     """
377:     Extract the section name text after removing number prefix and emoji.
378: 
379:     Examples:
380:         "1. 📖 Overview" -> "Overview"
381:         "📖 OVERVIEW" -> "OVERVIEW"
382:         "1. Overview" -> "Overview"

392: # Patterns that separate a legitimate mixed-case token (a code identifier or a
393: # product/acronym name) from a header that simply was not uppercased. Each
394: # requires a lowercase run to follow every internal capital, so a scrambled word
395: # like "oVERVIEW" or "tITLE" — a lone lowercase letter in front of an all-caps
396: # run — matches none of them and is correctly rejected.
397: _CAMEL_CASE = re.compile(r'[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:[A-Z][a-z0-9]+)+')       # renderBlocks, gate3Precedence
398: # Two or more capitalized segments: a single one (e.g. "Overview") is just a
399: # Title-Case word that must be uppercased, not a product name.
400: _PASCAL_CASE = re.compile(r'(?:[A-Z][a-z0-9]+){2,}')                  # JavaScript, OpenCode, MiMo
401: _ACRONYM_SUFFIX = re.compile(r'[A-Z]{2,}[a-z0-9]*')                   # OAuth, PDFs, AIs, HTTPStatus
402: # Irregular lowercase-first product names that no structural pattern can tell
403: # apart from garbage; keep this list explicit and small.
404: _PROPER_NOUN_WHITELIST = {'iOS', 'iPadOS', 'macOS', 'eBay', 'iPhone'}
405: 
406: 
407: def _is_identifier_or_proper_noun(token: str) -> bool:
408:     """A mixed-case token that is a code identifier or a product/acronym name."""
409:     return bool(
410:         _CAMEL_CASE.fullmatch(token)
411:         or _PASCAL_CASE.fullmatch(token)
412:         or _ACRONYM_SUFFIX.fullmatch(token)
413:         or token in _PROPER_NOUN_WHITELIST
414:     )

417: def _strip_nonprose(text: str) -> str:
418:     """
419:     Remove the parts of a header the ALL-CAPS rule must not police: code spans,
420:     autolinks, inline-link destinations (keeping the visible label), and balanced
421:     parenthetical groups (annotations and function-call args). Parentheses are
422:     matched by depth so a header like "API (legacy (v2) only)" is fully removed
423:     and a link whose URL itself contains parentheses never leaks a fragment — the
424:     two failure modes the earlier first-closing-paren regex got wrong.
425:     """
426:     text = re.sub(r'`[^`]*`', ' ', text)   # inline code spans first
427:     out = []
428:     i, n = 0, len(text)
429:     while i < n:
430:         ch = text[i]
431:         if ch == '<':                       # autolink <https://...>
432:             j = text.find('>', i + 1)
433:             if j != -1:
434:                 out.append(' ')
435:                 i = j + 1
436:                 continue
437:         if ch == '[':                       # inline link [label](url): keep label, drop the URL
438:             close = text.find(']', i + 1)
439:             if close != -1 and close + 1 < n and text[close + 1] == '(':
440:                 out.append(' ' + text[i + 1:close] + ' ')
441:                 depth, k = 0, close + 1
442:                 while k < n:
443:                     if text[k] == '(':
444:                         depth += 1
445:                     elif text[k] == ')':
446:                         depth -= 1
447:                         if depth == 0:
448:                             k += 1
449:                             break
450:                     k += 1
451:                 i = k
452:                 continue
453:         if ch == '(':                       # function call, or a parenthetical annotation
454:             # A '(' with an identifier immediately before it (no space) is a
455:             # function name plus args, so drop the name too; a space before it
456:             # means a prose word followed by a parenthetical, so keep the word.
457:             while out and (out[-1].isalnum() or out[-1] in '_.'):
458:                 out.pop()
459:             depth, k = 0, i
460:             while k < n:
461:                 if text[k] == '(':
462:                     depth += 1
463:                 elif text[k] == ')':
464:                     depth -= 1
465:                     if depth == 0:
466:                         k += 1
467:                         break
468:                 k += 1
469:             out.append(' ')
470:             i = k
471:             continue
472:         out.append(ch)
473:         i += 1
474:     return ''.join(out)
475:

477: def is_uppercase_section(text: str) -> bool:
478:     """
479:     Check whether a section name satisfies the ALL-CAPS rule.
480: 
481:     The rule applies to prose words only. Code spans, parenthetical annotations,
482:     function-call args, and link destinations are removed first; a code
483:     identifier (camelCase) or a product/acronym name (PascalCase, OAuth, PDFs)
484:     is then accepted as-is. A header fails only when a plain prose word is
485:     Title-Case, all-lowercase, or scrambled mixed-case.
486: 
487:     Examples:
488:         "OVERVIEW" -> True
489:         "Overview" -> False
490:         "oVERVIEW" -> False
491:         "INSTALLATION & SETUP" -> True
492:         "MODE DETECTION (`SP-001..SP-004`)" -> True
493:         "DEPTH LOOP renderBlocks" -> True
494:         "API (legacy (v2) only)" -> True
495:         "API <https://example.com/docs>" -> True
496:     """
497:     section_name = extract_section_name_text(text)
498:     for raw in re.split(r'[\s/,:;.\-—–&\'"?!→|]+', _strip_nonprose(section_name)):
499:         token = raw.strip('`()[]{}\'".,:;<>')
500:         letters = [c for c in token if c.isalpha()]
501:         if len(letters) < 2:
502:             continue
503:         if ''.join(letters).isupper():
504:             continue                       # ALL-CAPS prose word: fine
505:         if _is_identifier_or_proper_noun(token):
506:             continue                       # code identifier or product/acronym name
507:         return False                       # Title-Case, lowercase, or scrambled prose word
508:     # Nothing prose remained to enforce the rule on.
509:     return True
510:

518:         "Quick Start" -> "QUICK START"
519:         "What's Next?" -> "WHAT'S NEXT?"

521:     return text.upper()

528: def validate_toc(content: str, doc_type_rules: Dict[str, Any], rules: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
529:     """Validate TABLE OF CONTENTS section."""
530:     errors = []
531: 
532:     if not doc_type_rules.get('tocRequired', False):
533:         return errors
534: 
535:     # Accept variations with emoji (📑) or without
536:     # Pattern: ## [optional emoji] TABLE OF CONTENTS
537:     toc_match = re.search(
538:         r'## (?:[^\w\s]\s+)?TABLE OF CONTENTS\s*\n(.*?)(?=\n---|\n## |\Z)',
539:         content,
540:         re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE
541:     )
542: 
543:     if not toc_match:
544:         errors.append({
545:             'type': 'missing_toc',
546:             'severity': 'blocking',
547:             'message': 'Missing TABLE OF CONTENTS section',
548:             'fix_hint': 'Add "## TABLE OF CONTENTS" section with linked entries'
549:         })
550:         return errors
551: 
552:     toc_content = toc_match.group(1)
553: 
554:     for line_num, line in enumerate(toc_content.strip().split('\n'), start=1):
555:         line = line.strip()
556:         if not line.startswith('- ['):
557:             continue
558: 
559:         # Double-dash anchors required for GitHub compatibility
560:         anchor_match = re.search(r'\(#(\d+)-([a-z])', line)
561:         if anchor_match:
562:             errors.append({
563:                 'type': 'toc_single_dash_anchor',
564:                 'severity': 'blocking',
565:                 'message': f'TOC anchor uses single dash instead of double dash',
566:                 'line': line,
567:                 'fix_hint': f'Change "#N-" to "#N--" in anchor',
568:                 'auto_fixable': True,
569:                 'fix': line.replace(f'#{anchor_match.group(1)}-', f'#{anchor_match.group(1)}--')
570:             })
571: 
572:         entry_match = re.search(r'\[(.+?)\]', line)
573:         if entry_match:
574:             entry_text = entry_match.group(1)
575: 
576:             # Check for ALL CAPS (only for readme type which requires it)
577:             uppercase_required = doc_type_rules.get('tocUppercaseRequired', False)
578:             if uppercase_required and not is_uppercase_section(entry_text):
579:                 section_text = extract_section_name_text(entry_text)
580:                 # Build fixed entry: preserve number and emoji, uppercase the name
581:                 # Pattern: "N. EMOJI name" -> "N. EMOJI NAME"
582:                 fixed_entry = re.sub(
583:                     r'^(\d+\.\s*)([^\w\s]\s*)?(.+)$',
584:                     lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2) or ''}{m.group(3).upper()}",
585:                     entry_text
586:                 )
587:                 fixed_line = line.replace(f'[{entry_text}]', f'[{fixed_entry}]')
588: 
589:                 errors.append({
590:                     'type': 'toc_not_uppercase',
591:                     'severity': 'blocking',
592:                     'message': f'TOC entry not ALL CAPS: "{entry_text}"',
593:                     'line': line,
594:                     'auto_fixable': True,
595:                     'fix': fixed_line,
596:                     'fix_hint': f'Change "{section_text}" to "{section_text.upper()}"'
597:                 })
598: 
599:     return errors

606: def _fenced_line_numbers(content: str) -> set:
607:     """1-based line numbers that fall inside fenced code blocks.
608: 
609:     Tracks the opening fence's backtick length so a longer outer fence (```` )
610:     keeps shorter inner fences (```) literal, and a closing fence must be at least
611:     as long as its opener with no info string. This is why a naive "any ``` opens,
612:     a bare ``` closes" scan mis-nests 4-backtick doc examples. Used so section
613:     numbering ignores numbered headers shown inside a copy-able template example —
614:     they are content, not document sections.
615:     """
616:     fenced = set()
617:     fence_len = 0
618:     for i, line in enumerate(content.split('\n'), start=1):
619:         stripped = line.strip()
620:         if stripped.startswith('```'):
621:             ticks = len(stripped) - len(stripped.lstrip('`'))
622:             info = stripped[ticks:].strip()
623:             fenced.add(i)
624:             if fence_len == 0:
625:                 fence_len = ticks
626:             elif ticks >= fence_len and info == '':
627:                 fence_len = 0
628:             continue
629:         if fence_len > 0:
630:             fenced.add(i)
631:     return fenced

392: # Patterns that separate a legitimate mixed-case token (a code identifier or a

397: _CAMEL_CASE = re.compile(r'[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:[A-Z][a-z0-9]+)+')       # renderBlocks, gate3Precedence

402: # Irregular lowercase-first product names that no structural pattern can tell
403: # apart from garbage; keep this list explicit and small.
