417: def _strip_nonprose(text: str) -> str:
418:     """
419:     Remove the parts of a header the ALL-CAPS rule must not police: code spans,
420:     autolinks, inline-link destinations (keeping the visible label), and balanced
421:     parenthetical groups (annotations and function-call args). Parentheses are
422:     matched by depth so a header like "API (legacy (v2) only)" is fully removed
423:     and a link whose URL itself contains parentheses never leaks a fragment — the
424:     two failure modes the earlier first-closing-paren regex got wrong.
425:     """
426:     text = re.sub(r'`[^`]*`', ' ', text)   # inline code spans first
427:     out = []
428:     i, n = 0, len(text)
429:     while i < n:
430:         ch = text[i]
431:         if ch == '<':                       # autolink <https://...>
432:             j = text.find('>', i + 1)
433:             if j != -1:
434:                 out.append(' ')
435:                 i = j + 1
436:                 continue
437:         if ch == '[':                       # inline link [label](url): keep label, drop the URL
438:             close = text.find(']', i + 1)
439:             if close != -1 and close + 1 < n and text[close + 1] == '(':
440:                 out.append(' ' + text[i + 1:close] + ' ')
441:                 depth, k = 0, close + 1
442:                 while k < n:
443:                     if text[k] == '(':
444:                         depth += 1
445:                     elif text[k] == ')':
446:                         depth -= 1
447:                         if depth == 0:
448:                             k += 1
449:                             break
450:                     k += 1
451:                 i = k
452:                 continue
453:         if ch == '(':                       # function call, or a parenthetical annotation
454:             # A '(' with an identifier immediately before it (no space) is a
455:             # function name plus args, so drop the name too; a space before it
456:             # means a prose word followed by a parenthetical, so keep the word.
457:             while out and (out[-1].isalnum() or out[-1] in '_.'):
458:                 out.pop()
459:             depth, k = 0, i
460:             while k < n:
461:                 if text[k] == '(':
462:                     depth += 1
463:                 elif text[k] == ')':
464:                     depth -= 1
465:                     if depth == 0:
466:                         k += 1
467:                         break
468:                 k += 1
469:             out.append(' ')
470:             i = k
471:             continue
472:         out.append(ch)
473:         i += 1
474:     return ''.join(out)

477: def is_uppercase_section(text: str) -> bool:
478:     """
479:     Check whether a section name satisfies the ALL-CAPS rule.
480: 
481:     The rule applies to prose words only. Code spans, parenthetical annotations,
482:     function-call args, and link destinations are removed first; a code
483:     identifier (camelCase) or a product/acronym name (PascalCase, OAuth, PDFs)
484:     is then accepted as-is. A header fails only when a plain prose word is
485:     Title-Case, all-lowercase, or scrambled mixed-case.
486: 
487:     Examples:
488:         "OVERVIEW" -> True
489:         "Overview" -> False
490:         "oVERVIEW" -> False
491:         "INSTALLATION & SETUP" -> True
492:         "MODE DETECTION (`SP-001..SP-004`)" -> True
493:         "DEPTH LOOP renderBlocks" -> True
494:         "API (legacy (v2) only)" -> True
495:         "API <https://example.com/docs>" -> True
496:     """
497:     section_name = extract_section_name_text(text)
498:     for raw in re.split(r'[\s/,:;.\-—–&\'"?!→|]+', _strip_nonprose(section_name)):
499:         token = raw.strip('`()[]{}\'".,:;<>')
500:         letters = [c for c in token if c.isalpha()]
501:         if len(letters) < 2:
502:             continue
503:         if ''.join(letters).isupper():
504:             continue                       # ALL-CAPS prose word: fine
505:         if _is_identifier_or_proper_noun(token):
506:             continue                       # code identifier or product/acronym name
507:         return False                       # Title-Case, lowercase, or scrambled prose word
508:     # Nothing prose remained to enforce the rule on.
509:     return True

528: def validate_toc(content: str, doc_type_rules: Dict[str, Any], rules: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
529:     """Validate TABLE OF CONTENTS section."""
530:     errors = []
531: 
532:     if not doc_type_rules.get('tocRequired', False):
533:         return errors
534: 
535:     # Accept variations with emoji (📑) or without
536:     # Pattern: ## [optional emoji] TABLE OF CONTENTS
537:     toc_match = re.search(
538:         r'## (?:[^\w\s]\s+)?TABLE OF CONTENTS\s*\n(.*?)(?=\n---|\n## |\Z)',
539:         content,
540:         re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE
541:     )
542: 
543:     if not toc_match:
544:         errors.append({
545:             'type': 'missing_toc',
546:             'severity': 'blocking',
547:             'message': 'Missing TABLE OF CONTENTS section',
548:             'fix_hint': 'Add "## TABLE OF CONTENTS" section with linked entries'
549:         })
550:         return errors
551: 
552:     toc_content = toc_match.group(1)
553: 
554:     for line_num, line in enumerate(toc_content.strip().split('\n'), start=1):
555:         line = line.strip()
556:         if not line.startswith('- ['):
557:             continue
558: 
559:         # Double-dash anchors required for GitHub compatibility
560:         anchor_match = re.search(r'\(#(\d+)-([a-z])', line)
561:         if anchor_match:
562:             errors.append({
563:                 'type': 'toc_single_dash_anchor',
564:                 'severity': 'blocking',
565:                 'message': f'TOC anchor uses single dash instead of double dash',
566:                 'line': line,
567:                 'fix_hint': f'Change "#N-" to "#N--" in anchor',
568:                 'auto_fixable': True,
569:                 'fix': line.replace(f'#{anchor_match.group(1)}-', f'#{anchor_match.group(1)}--')
570:             })
571: 
572:         entry_match = re.search(r'\[(.+?)\]', line)
573:         if entry_match:
574:             entry_text = entry_match.group(1)
575: 
576:             # Check for ALL CAPS (only for readme type which requires it)
577:             uppercase_required = doc_type_rules.get('tocUppercaseRequired', False)
578:             if uppercase_required and not is_uppercase_section(entry_text):
579:                 section_text = extract_section_name_text(entry_text)
580:                 # Build fixed entry: preserve number and emoji, uppercase the name
581:                 # Pattern: "N. EMOJI name" -> "N. EMOJI NAME"
582:                 fixed_entry = re.sub(
583:                     r'^(\d+\.\s*)([^\w\s]\s*)?(.+)$',
584:                     lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2) or ''}{m.group(3).upper()}",
585:                     entry_text
586:                 )
587:                 fixed_line = line.replace(f'[{entry_text}]', f'[{fixed_entry}]')
588: 
589:                 errors.append({
590:                     'type': 'toc_not_uppercase',
591:                     'severity': 'blocking',
592:                     'message': f'TOC entry not ALL CAPS: "{entry_text}"',
593:                     'line': line,
594:                     'auto_fixable': True,
595:                     'fix': fixed_line,
596:                     'fix_hint': f'Change "{section_text}" to "{section_text.upper()}"'
597:                 })
598: 
599:     return errors

606: def _fenced_line_numbers(content: str) -> set:
607:     """1-based line numbers that fall inside fenced code blocks.
608: 
609:     Tracks the opening fence's backtick length so a longer outer fence (```` )
610:     keeps shorter inner fences (```) literal, and a closing fence must be at least
611:     as long as its opener with no info string. This is why a naive "any ``` opens,
612:     a bare ``` closes" scan mis-nests 4-backtick doc examples. Used so section
613:     numbering ignores numbered headers shown inside a copy-able template example —
614:     they are content, not document sections.
615:     """
616:     fenced = set()
617:     fence_len = 0
618:     for i, line in enumerate(content.split('\n'), start=1):
619:         stripped = line.strip()
620:         if stripped.startswith('```'):
621:             ticks = len(stripped) - len(stripped.lstrip('`'))
622:             info = stripped[ticks:].strip()
623:             fenced.add(i)
624:             if fence_len == 0:
625:                 fence_len = ticks
626:             elif ticks >= fence_len and info == '':
627:                 fence_len = 0
628:             continue
629:         if fence_len > 0:
630:             fenced.add(i)
631:     return fenced

637: def is_repo_root_readme(file_path: str) -> bool:
638:     """Whether the file is the README at a repository root, the directory that holds
639:     `.git` (a folder in a checkout, a file in a linked worktree). That README separates
640:     its sections with ` ` lines instead of `---` rules, so the divider rule skips it."""
641:     path = Path(file_path).resolve()
642:     return path.name.lower() == 'readme.md' and (path.parent / '.git').exists()

645: def _structure_enforcement_enabled() -> bool:
646:     """Whether the general-path structure rules are enforced: a `---` divider between
647:     numbered ALL-CAPS H2 sections, no Table of Contents, and no navigation-anchor
648:     comments. Enforced by default. Set SKDOC_ENFORCE_STRUCTURE=0 to opt out, e.g. while
649:     migrating a doc set whose section structure has not been normalized yet."""
650:     return os.environ.get(_STRUCTURE_ENFORCEMENT_ENV, '1') != '0'
651:

653: def _transparent_structure_line(line: str) -> bool:
654:     """Return whether a line is transparent when checking a section boundary."""
655:     stripped = line.strip()
656:     return not stripped or bool(re.fullmatch(r'<!--.*-->', stripped))
657: 
658: 
659: def _section_caps_ignoring_qualifier(title: str) -> bool:
660:     """A numbered H2 counts as a section heading when its text, minus any parenthetical
661:     qualifier, is uppercase. This keeps headings like "FILE-LAYER SURFACE (what the AI
662:     edits)" in scope while leaving genuinely title-case headings out."""
663:     core = re.sub(r'\([^)]*\)', '', title).strip()
664:     return bool(core) and core == core.upper()

667: def validate_general_structure(content: str, doc_type_rules: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
668:     """Validate staged divider and navigation rules for the general path."""
669:     if not _structure_enforcement_enabled():
670:         return []
671: 
672:     errors: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
673:     lines = content.splitlines()
674:     fenced_lines = _fenced_line_numbers(content)
675: 
676:     if doc_type_rules.get('h2DividerRequired', False):
677:         h2_pattern = re.compile(r'^##\s+(\d+)\.\s+(.+?)\s*$')
678:         numbered_h2_lines = []
679:         for line_number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
680:             if line_number in fenced_lines:
681:                 continue
682:             match = h2_pattern.match(line)
683:             if match and _section_caps_ignoring_qualifier(match.group(2)):
684:                 numbered_h2_lines.append(line_number)
685: 
686:         for line_number in numbered_h2_lines[1:]:
687:             previous = line_number - 1
688:             while previous > 0 and _transparent_structure_line(lines[previous - 1]):
689:                 previous -= 1
690:             if previous == 0 or lines[previous - 1].strip() != '---':
691:                 errors.append({
692:                     'type': 'general_h2_separator',
693:                     'rule_id': 'general_h2_separator',
694:                     'severity': 'blocking',
695:                     'message': 'Numbered ALL-CAPS H2 sections must be separated by `---`.',
696:                     'line': lines[line_number - 1],
697:                     'line_number': line_number,
698:                     'fix_hint': 'Add `---` immediately above the numbered H2 section.',
699:                 })
700: 
701:     outside_body = '\n'.join(
702:         line for line_number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1)
703:         if line_number not in fenced_lines
704:     )
705:     if doc_type_rules.get('tocForbidden', False) and re.search(
706:         r'(?im)^\s*(?:#{1,6}\s+)?(?:\d+\.\s+)?TABLE OF CONTENTS\b',
707:         outside_body,
708:     ):
709:         errors.append({
710:             'type': 'general_no_toc',
711:             'rule_id': 'general_no_toc',
712:             'severity': 'blocking',
713:             'message': 'This document type must not contain a Table of Contents.',
714:             'fix_hint': 'Remove the Table of Contents and use numbered H2 sections for navigation.',
715:         })
716:     if doc_type_rules.get('anchorNavigationForbidden', False) and re.search(
717:         r'^[ \t]*<!--[ \t]*/?ANCHOR:[^>\r\n]*-->[ \t]*$',
718:         outside_body,
719:         re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE,
720:     ):
721:         errors.append({
722:             'type': 'general_no_anchor',
723:             'rule_id': 'general_no_anchor',
724:             'severity': 'blocking',
725:             'message': 'This document type must not contain anchor-comment navigation.',
726:             'fix_hint': 'Remove navigation anchor comments and use numbered H2 sections instead.',
727:         })
728: 
729:     return errors

732: def validate_h2_headers(content: str, doc_type_rules: Dict[str, Any], rules: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
733:     """Validate H2 header format and emojis."""
734:     errors = []
735: 
736:     h2_pattern = re.compile(r'^## (\d+)\.\s+(.+)$', re.MULTILINE)
737:     matches = list(h2_pattern.finditer(content))
738:     fenced_lines = _fenced_line_numbers(content)
739: 
740:     if not matches:
741:         # No numbered H2 headers found - check if this is expected
742:         # Some documents might use different header styles
743:         return errors
744: 
745:     expected_num = 1
746:     emoji_required = doc_type_rules.get('h2EmojiRequired', True)
747:     section_emojis = doc_type_rules.get('sectionEmojis', {})
748:     section_aliases = doc_type_rules.get('sectionAliases', {})
749: 
750:     for match in matches:
751:         num = int(match.group(1))
752:         title = match.group(2).strip()
753:         line = match.group(0)
754: 
755:         # A numbered header inside a fenced example (a copy-able skeleton) is
756:         # content, not a section, so it must not break or advance the outer
757:         # document sequence. Emoji/uppercase checks below intentionally still
758:         # apply to every match, keeping their behavior unchanged.
759:         header_line = content.count('\n', 0, match.start()) + 1
760:         if header_line not in fenced_lines:
761:             if num != expected_num:
762:                 errors.append({
763:                     'type': 'non_sequential_numbering',
764:                     'severity': 'warning',
765:                     'message': f'Non-sequential section number: expected {expected_num}, found {num}',
766:                     'line': line
767:                 })
768:             expected_num = num + 1
769: 
770:         if emoji_required:
771:             title_has_emoji = has_emoji(title)
772: 
773:             if not title_has_emoji:
774:                 section_name = normalize_section_name(title)
775: 
776:                 if section_name in section_aliases:
777:                     section_name = section_aliases[section_name]
778: 
779:                 expected_emoji = section_emojis.get(section_name)
780: 
781:                 # Fallback: match ignoring underscores for flexibility
782:                 if not expected_emoji:
783:                     section_name_no_underscore = section_name.replace('_', '')
784:                     for key, emoji in section_emojis.items():
785:                         if key.replace('_', '') == section_name_no_underscore:
786:                             expected_emoji = emoji
787:                             break
788: 
789:                 errors.append({
790:                     'type': 'missing_h2_emoji',
791:                     'severity': 'blocking',
792:                     'message': f'H2 header missing emoji: "{line}"',
793:                     'line': line,
794:                     'section_name': section_name,
795:                     'expected_emoji': expected_emoji,
796:                     'auto_fixable': expected_emoji is not None,
797:                     'fix': f'## {num}. {expected_emoji} {title}' if expected_emoji else None,
798:                     'fix_hint': f'Add {expected_emoji} after "{num}."' if expected_emoji else 'Add appropriate emoji after section number'
799:                 })
800: 
801:         # Check for ALL CAPS (only for document types that require it)
802:         uppercase_required = doc_type_rules.get('h2UppercaseRequired', False)
803:         if uppercase_required and not is_uppercase_section(title):
804:             section_text = extract_section_name_text(title)
805:             # Extract emoji if present
806:             emoji = extract_first_emoji(title)
807: 
808:             if emoji:
809:                 # Has emoji: "EMOJI name" -> "EMOJI NAME"
810:                 title_after_emoji = EMOJI_PATTERN.sub('', title).strip()
811:                 fixed_title = f'{emoji} {title_after_emoji.upper()}'
812:             else:
813:                 # No emoji: just uppercase
814:                 fixed_title = title.upper()
815: 
816:             errors.append({
817:                 'type': 'h2_not_uppercase',
818:                 'severity': 'blocking',
819:                 'message': f'H2 header not ALL CAPS: "{line}"',
820:                 'line': line,
821:                 'auto_fixable': True,
822:                 'fix': f'## {num}. {fixed_title}',
823:                 'fix_hint': f'Change "{section_text}" to "{section_text.upper()}"'
824:             })
825: 
826:     return errors

833: def validate_required_sections(content: str, doc_type_rules: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
834:     """Check that required sections are present."""
835:     errors = []
836: 
837:     required = doc_type_rules.get('requiredSections', [])
838:     section_aliases = doc_type_rules.get('sectionAliases', {})
839: 
840:     # Compiled-contract commands are thin runtime dispatchers whose section content is
841:     # rendered from a compiled source at invocation, not written in the .md file, so
842:     # there is no prose section shape to require here.
843:     contract_marker = doc_type_rules.get('compiledContractMarker')
844:     if contract_marker and contract_marker in content:
845:         return errors
846: 
847:     # Build reverse alias map
848:     reverse_aliases = {}
849:     for alias, canonical in section_aliases.items():
850:         reverse_aliases.setdefault(canonical, []).append(alias)
851: 
852:     h2_pattern = re.compile(r'^## \d+\.\s+[^\n]+', re.MULTILINE)
853:     headers = h2_pattern.findall(content)
854: 
855:     # Keep both normalized and raw names for partial matching fallback
856:     found_sections = set()
857:     found_sections_raw = []
858:     for header in headers:
859:         match = re.search(r'^## \d+\.\s+(?:[^\w\s]\s+)?(.+)$', header)
860:         if match:
861:             raw_name = match.group(1).strip().lower()
862:             section_name = normalize_section_name(raw_name)
863:             found_sections.add(section_name)
864:             found_sections_raw.append(raw_name)
865: 
866:             if section_name in section_aliases:
867:                 found_sections.add(section_aliases[section_name])
868: 
869:     # A router command is a thin dispatcher (verify agent -> resolve mode/args -> hand
870:     # off to owned presentation/workflow assets). It carries a router-specific section
871:     # vocabulary instead of the general purpose/instructions sections, so detect that
872:     # shape and require only the minimal router core, treating the rest as recommended.
873:     # A section counts as present if its canonical name is a found header OR a known
874:     # space-form alias of it normalizes (space->underscore) to a found header.
875:     def section_present(canonical: str) -> bool:
876:         if canonical in found_sections:
877:             return True
878:         for alias in reverse_aliases.get(canonical, []):
879:             if alias.replace(' ', '_') in found_sections:
880:                 return True
881:         return False
882: 
883:     detect_primary = doc_type_rules.get('routerDetectPrimary', [])
884:     structural = doc_type_rules.get('routerStructuralSections', [])
885:     is_router = (
886:         any(section_present(sig) for sig in detect_primary)
887:         or sum(1 for sig in structural if section_present(sig)) >= 2
888:     )
889:     if is_router:
890:         required = doc_type_rules.get('routerRequiredSections', required)
891: 
892:     # A surface packet is a read-only evidence base a parent hub bundles beside a
893:     # workflow mode, not a workflow of its own, so it carries no WHEN TO USE, SMART
894:     # ROUTING or HOW IT WORKS. Its opening section says when the hub bundles it, which
895:     # marks the shape, and the packet is held to its evidence core instead.
896:     if any(section_present(sig) for sig in doc_type_rules.get('surfaceDetectPrimary', [])):
897:         required = doc_type_rules.get('surfaceRequiredSections', required)
898: 
899:     for req_section in required:
900:         found = req_section in found_sections
901: 
902:         if not found:
903:             aliases = reverse_aliases.get(req_section, [])
904:             for alias in aliases:
905:                 if alias.replace(' ', '_') in found_sections:
906:                     found = True
907:                     break
908: 
909:         # Fuzzy match: accept if all required words appear in section name
910:         if not found:
911:             req_words = req_section.replace('_', ' ').split()
912:             for raw_section in found_sections_raw:
913:                 if all(word in raw_section for word in req_words):
914:                     found = True
915:                     break
916: 
917:         if not found:
918:             errors.append({
919:                 'type': 'missing_required_section',
920:                 'severity': 'blocking',
921:                 'message': f'Missing required section: {req_section}',
922:                 'fix_hint': f'Add section with name containing "{req_section}"'
923:             })
924: 
925:     # Router shape beyond the minimal core is recommended, not required: surface any
926:     # missing canonical router section as a non-blocking warning so authors converge on
927:     # the full vocabulary without failing incremental migrations.
928:     if is_router:
929:         for rec_section in doc_type_rules.get('routerRecommendedSections', []):
930:             if not section_present(rec_section):
931:                 errors.append({
932:                     'type': 'missing_recommended_router_section',
933:                     'severity': 'warning',
934:                     'message': f'Missing recommended router section: {rec_section}',
935:                     'fix_hint': f'Add a "{rec_section}" section (recommended for router commands)'
936:                 })
937: 
938:     return errors
939:

945: def apply_fixes(content: str, errors: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Tuple[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
946:     """
947:     Apply auto-fixes to content.
948: 
949:     Uses iterative approach: after each fix, re-validates and applies more fixes
950:     until no more fixes can be applied. This handles cases where multiple fixes
951:     affect the same line (e.g., single-dash anchor AND missing emoji).
952:     """
953:     fixed_content = content
954:     all_fixes_applied = []
955:     max_iterations = 10  # Safety limit
956: 
957:     for iteration in range(max_iterations):
958:         fixes_this_round = []
959: 
960:         for error in errors:
961:             if not error.get('auto_fixable'):
962:                 continue
963: 
964:             fix = error.get('fix')
965:             original = error.get('line')
966: 
967:             if fix and original and original in fixed_content:
968:                 fixed_content = fixed_content.replace(original, fix, 1)
969:                 fixes_this_round.append({
970:                     'type': error['type'],
971:                     'original': original,
972:                     'fixed': fix
973:                 })
974: 
975:         if not fixes_this_round:
976:             # No more fixes could be applied
977:             break
978: 
979:         all_fixes_applied.extend(fixes_this_round)
980: 
981:         # Re-validate to get updated error list with new line content
982:         # This allows subsequent fixes to find the modified lines
983:         # Re-run validation on the fixed content to get fresh errors
984:         script_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
985:         rules = load_template_rules(script_dir)
986: 
987:         # Detect doc type from original errors or default to readme
988:         doc_type = 'readme'
989:         for e in errors:
990:             if 'skill' in str(e.get('line', '')).lower():
991:                 doc_type = 'skill'
992:                 break
993: 
994:         # Get fresh errors based on current fixed content
995:         doc_type_rules = rules.get('documentTypes', {}).get(doc_type, {})
996:         errors = []
997:         errors.extend(validate_toc(fixed_content, doc_type_rules, rules))
998:         errors.extend(validate_h2_headers(fixed_content, doc_type_rules, rules))
999: 
1000:     return fixed_content, all_fixes_applied

1016: def _code_folder_fence_lines(content: str) -> Tuple[set, List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
1017:     """Return fenced lines and errors for untagged fenced blocks."""
1018:     fenced: set = set()
1019:     errors: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
1020:     opening_line: Optional[int] = None
1021:     opening_ticks = 0
1022:     opening_info = ''
1023: 
1024:     for line_number, line in enumerate(content.splitlines(), start=1):
1025:         match = re.match(r'^\s*(`{3,})(.*)$', line)
1026:         if not match:
1027:             if opening_line is not None:
1028:                 fenced.add(line_number)
1029:             continue
1030: 
1031:         ticks = len(match.group(1))
1032:         info = match.group(2).strip()
1033:         fenced.add(line_number)
1034:         if opening_line is None:
1035:             opening_line = line_number
1036:             opening_ticks = ticks
1037:             opening_info = info
1038:             if not info:
1039:                 errors.append({
1040:                     'type': 'code_folder_fence_language',
1041:                     'rule_id': 'code_folder_fence_language',
1042:                     'severity': 'blocking',
1043:                     'message': 'Fenced code block is missing a language tag.',
1044:                     'line': line,
1045:                     'line_number': line_number,
1046:                     'fix_hint': 'Add a language tag after the opening fence.',
1047:                 })
1048:         elif ticks >= opening_ticks and not info:
1049:             opening_line = None
1050:             opening_ticks = 0
1051:             opening_info = ''
1052: 
1053:     if opening_line is not None:
1054:         errors.append({
1055:             'type': 'code_folder_fence_language',
1056:             'rule_id': 'code_folder_fence_language',
1057:             'severity': 'blocking',
1058:             'message': 'Fenced code block is not closed.',
1059:             'line_number': opening_line,
1060:             'fix_hint': 'Close the fenced code block.',
1061:         })
1062: 
1063:     return fenced, errors

1090:     has_inventory_heading = bool(re.search(

---
title: Web Accessibility Patterns
description: Widget contracts, focus handling and browser accessibility preferences for web interfaces.
trigger_phrases:
  - "web accessibility patterns"
  - "aria widget keyboard behavior"
  - "browser accessibility preferences"
importance_tier: important
contextType: implementation
version: 1.0.1.0
---

# Web Accessibility Patterns

Widget contracts, focus handling and browser accessibility preferences for web interfaces.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

This file covers widget behavior, focus and browser accessibility preferences. Support summaries use the web-features Baseline classifications and browser-version data.

### When to Use

- Adding or changing a modal dialog
- Mapping a component library's behavior to a widget pattern
- Naming controls or moving focus
- Adding announcements or honoring browser accessibility preferences
- Building a widget pattern or wiring form validation and error messages

### Boundaries

- Native element choice and baseline semantics: [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
- State selectors such as `:focus-visible`: [web-cascade-and-selectors.md](web-cascade-and-selectors.md).
- Element and attribute mechanics for dialogs, popovers and forms: [web-elements-and-attributes.md](web-elements-and-attributes.md).

---

## 2. MODAL DIALOG CONTRACT

### A1. Modal dialog

- **Rule:** Use native `<dialog>` with `showModal()` or a component library's documented modal behavior.
- **Why:** These mechanisms provide top-layer placement, Escape handling, focus containment and an inert background.
- **When not to:** Use a non-modal dialog when the surrounding page must remain interactive.
- **Pitfall:** Setting `aria-modal="true"` on an ordinary element hides the rest of the page from assistive technology without making the page inert.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `dialog`). Chrome 37 / Firefox 98 / Safari 15.4.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Dialog (modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)

---

## 3. LIBRARY MAPPING

| Pattern | Integration boundary |
|---|---|
| Modal dialog | Close through the dialog lifecycle so focus returns to the opener. |
| Menu button | Use a disclosure and navigation list for site navigation; a menu role promises menu keyboard behavior. |
| Tabs, listbox or combobox | Do not add tabindex values or arrow-key handlers when a component manages roving focus; treat its autocomplete as a combobox and do not redeclare supplied roles. |
| Accordion, disclosure or tooltip | Keep expanded state aligned; disabled controls may not receive focus, and a tooltip cannot be the only label. |
| Status region, table or grid | Keep the live region mounted before changing its text; set `aria-sort` on the sorted header when needed. |
| Focus styling | Keep a visible replacement if an outline is removed. |

When a component library provides widget roles, state, focus movement or announcements, use that behavior as the source of truth. For hand-written widgets, implement the complete pattern described below.

---

## 4. NAMES AND FOCUS

### A2. Accessible name order

- **Rule:** Prefer `aria-labelledby` that points to visible text, and preserve the order `aria-labelledby`, `aria-label`, host-language label, then `title`.
- **Why:** A higher-priority naming source replaces lower-priority sources in the computed accessible name.
- **When not to:** Omit ARIA naming attributes when a native label already provides the intended name.
- **Pitfall:** An `aria-label` of `Send` replaces visible `Submit` text and can break speech input that uses the visible label.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: Accessible name calculation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Guides/Accessible_name_calculation)

### A3. Roving tabindex and active descendant

- **Rule:** Use roving tabindex for items that move DOM focus, and use `aria-activedescendant` when focus stays on a text input.
- **Why:** Roving tabindex moves browser focus, while `aria-activedescendant` exposes an active child without moving focus from its owner.
- **When not to:** Use neither pattern for ordinary links or buttons that already provide the needed keyboard behavior.
- **Pitfall:** The active descendant must reference a rendered element with a stable ID, so virtualized options can leave a dangling reference.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/)

### A4. Focus return through the dialog reference

- **Rule:** Close a library-managed overlay through its documented lifecycle so it can restore focus to the opener.
- **Why:** The component lifecycle can return focus after the modal leaves the top layer.
- **When not to:** Focus a logical successor when the opener no longer exists after the interaction.
- **Pitfall:** Removing a dialog through application state can bypass the component lifecycle and leave focus on `body`.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Dialog (modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)

### A5. Focus-visible styling

- **Rule:** Use `:focus-visible` for browser-selected focus styling and retain a clear keyboard focus indicator.
- **Why:** The browser tracks input modality and matches the selector when it determines a focus indicator is needed. Use [CS9](web-cascade-and-selectors.md#cs9-existing-state-selector-contract) for the state-selector contract that applies to focus styling.
- **When not to:** Add an explicit focus state when a programmatic focus change must always display a ring.
- **Pitfall:** Programmatic focus may not match `:focus-visible`, even when the newly focused container needs an indicator.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `focus-visible`). Chrome 86 / Firefox 85 / Safari 15.4.
- **See also:** [MDN: :focus-visible](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:focus-visible)

### A6. Inert background

- **Rule:** Set `inert` on the background while a custom modal is open, and leave the modal subtree interactive.
- **Why:** Inert removes descendants from sequential focus and interaction, while `aria-hidden` only changes the accessibility tree.
- **When not to:** Do not set `inert` when the surface is a non-modal overlay that leaves the page usable.
- **Pitfall:** Applying `inert` to the overlay itself makes its controls unreachable.
- **Support:** See [EA4](web-elements-and-attributes.md#ea4-inert-background-boundary) for browser support.
- **See also:** [MDN: inert global attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/inert)

---

## 5. ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PREFERENCES

### A7. Live-region timing

- **Rule:** Mount a live-region container before updating its text, set `aria-atomic="true"` when the whole message must be read and reserve assertive announcements for interrupting errors.
- **Why:** Assistive technology observes changes to an existing live region and may miss a region created with its first message.
- **When not to:** Do not add a live region to content already announced through ordinary navigation or focus movement.
- **Pitfall:** Recreating an alert region for each render can repeat the same message or fail to announce it.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: aria-live](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-live)

### A8. Forced colors

- **Rule:** Use system colors such as `Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `Highlight` and `HighlightText` for essential text, and use borders rather than shadows for boundaries in forced-colors mode.
- **Why:** The browser can replace author colors and remove background images when forced colors are active.
- **When not to:** Use `forced-color-adjust: none` only when preserving a specific color is necessary to convey meaning.
- **Pitfall:** Hard-coded SVG fills and shadow-only borders can disappear from the high-contrast presentation.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-03-12 (web-features `forced-colors`). Chrome 89 / Firefox 89 / Safari 16.
- **See also:** [MDN: forced-colors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors)

### A9. Reduced motion

- **Rule:** Put optional motion inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` and keep progress feedback available in both modes.
- **Why:** The default path remains safe when the preference is unknown or reduced, while the opt-in applies motion only to users who allow it.
- **When not to:** Do not add an animation when a state change is already clear without motion.
- **Pitfall:** A global animation reset can remove a loading spinner and leave no visible progress cue.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `prefers-reduced-motion`). Chrome 74 / Firefox 63 / Safari 10.1.
- **See also:** [MDN: prefers-reduced-motion](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion)

### A10. Contrast, color scheme and transparency preferences

- **Rule:** Set `color-scheme` for supported themes, honor contrast preferences, and treat reduced-transparency styling as a feature-detected enhancement over an opaque baseline.
- **Why:** The media preferences expose user display choices, while `color-scheme` lets browser controls adapt to the declared theme.
- **When not to:** Keep the opaque baseline when the interface has no transparency effect to reduce.
- **Pitfall:** Depending on `prefers-reduced-transparency` alone leaves Safari users without the fallback, and Firefox support requires a preference flag.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-11-30 (web-features `prefers-contrast`). Chrome 96 / Firefox 101 / Safari 14.1. Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `prefers-color-scheme`). Chrome 76 / Firefox 67 / Safari 12.1. Baseline widely available since 2024-08-03 (web-features `color-scheme`). Chrome 98 / Firefox 96 / Safari 13. Baseline limited availability (web-features `prefers-reduced-transparency`). Chrome 119 / Firefox unsupported / Safari unsupported.
- **See also:** [MDN: prefers-contrast](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-contrast)

---

## 6. WIDGET PATTERNS

### A11. Carousel

- **Rule:** Provide a visible rotation control, pause rotation on hover and focus and set `aria-live="off"` while it rotates.
- **Why:** Rotation changes content without user input, so a pause control and controlled announcements preserve predictable navigation.
- **When not to:** Omit rotation controls when the carousel never rotates automatically.
- **Pitfall:** Previous and next buttons without labels leave their direction unclear to screen-reader users.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Carousel](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/)

### A12. Table and grid

- **Rule:** Use a native table for static data and use `role="grid"` only when the widget implements its full keyboard interaction model.
- **Why:** A grid role promises managed focus and keyboard navigation beyond a table's row and column relationships.
- **When not to:** Use a grid when users edit, select or navigate cells as an interactive widget.
- **Pitfall:** A sortable table needs `aria-sort` on the currently sorted header.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Grid](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/)

### A13. Menu button

- **Rule:** Pair `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded` with Up or Down to open, Home and End, typeahead, Escape to close and return focus and Tab to close.
- **Why:** The menu-button pattern exposes a popup menu whose items use composite-widget keyboard behavior.
- **When not to:** Use a disclosure button and navigation list for site navigation.
- **Pitfall:** Applying `role="menu"` to ordinary site navigation changes assistive-technology expectations without supplying menu keyboard behavior.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Menu button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/)

### A14. Tooltip

- **Rule:** Give supplemental content `role="tooltip"`, associate its trigger through `aria-describedby`, show it on hover and focus and let Escape dismiss it.
- **Why:** The described-by relationship makes the tooltip's supplemental text available when the trigger receives focus.
- **When not to:** Use a dialog or popover when the content contains interactive controls.
- **Pitfall:** A tooltip on a disabled control may never appear, and a tooltip cannot provide the control's only name.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Tooltip](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/)

---

## 7. FORMS AND VALIDATION

### A15. Framework validation layers

- **Rule:** For forms handled by a framework validation layer, render app feedback and confirm whether the framework disables native browser validation. Keep native constraint attributes so the framework can read them.
- **Why:** A framework may add `novalidate` or otherwise replace browser validation bubbles while still using attributes such as `required` and `min` as validator inputs.
- **When not to:** Use browser-native validation when its message UI is the intended path.
- **Pitfall:** `setCustomValidity()` does not restore browser validation UI while `novalidate` remains on the form.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: Constraint validation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Constraint_validation)

### A16. Error association in library and hand-written fields

- **Rule:** Inside a component library's form-field wrapper, let the library associate its error and hint messages. In a hand-written field, bind the visible message ID and invalid state to the control.
- **Why:** A library may add message IDs to the input's `aria-describedby` list and update its `aria-invalid` state. For a hand-written field, give each message an ID, reference it from the control and set the invalid state when validation fails.
- **When not to:** Do not add a duplicate `aria-describedby` ID or invalid-state binding when the component already manages both.
- **Pitfall:** A library may show an error when a control is invalid and touched or when the form is submitted. A hand-written component that shows errors only when dirty behaves differently.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI: Forms tutorial, notifications](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/)

### A17. Error summary and focus on submit

- **Rule:** After a failed submit, focus the first invalid control or an error summary that links to each invalid control.
- **Why:** The summary gives assistive technology users one place to review errors and jump to the affected fields.
- **When not to:** A single-field form, such as a search box, can keep focus on its field and show the inline error there.
- **Pitfall:** After a submit handler marks every control as touched, focus remains on the submit button unless code moves it. Newly rendered error text is not automatically announced.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI: Forms tutorial, notifications](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/)

### A18. Async validator pending state

- **Rule:** Block submission while a form is pending as well as when it is invalid. Expose validation progress with `aria-busy` on the field group or a polite status message.
- **Why:** An asynchronous validator can leave a form pending while both its valid and invalid states are false.
- **When not to:** A form with no async validators needs only the `invalid` check.
- **Pitfall:** A submit check that reads only `form.invalid` can run before async validation finishes. A disabled control leaves the tab order and is excluded from the form's aggregate value.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: Constraint validation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Constraint_validation)

# Web Accessibility Patterns

Widget contracts, focus handling and browser accessibility preferences for web interfaces.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

This file covers widget behavior, focus and browser accessibility preferences. Support summaries use the web-features Baseline classifications and browser-version data.

### When to Use

- Adding or changing a modal dialog
- Mapping a component library's behavior to a widget pattern
- Naming controls or moving focus
- Adding announcements or honoring browser accessibility preferences
- Building a widget pattern or wiring form validation and error messages

### Boundaries

- Native element choice and baseline semantics: [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
- State selectors such as `:focus-visible`: [web-cascade-and-selectors.md](web-cascade-and-selectors.md).
- Element and attribute mechanics for dialogs, popovers and forms: [web-elements-and-attributes.md](web-elements-and-attributes.md).

---

## 2. MODAL DIALOG CONTRACT

### A1. Modal dialog

- **Rule:** Use native `<dialog>` with `showModal()` or a component library's documented modal behavior.
- **Why:** These mechanisms provide top-layer placement, Escape handling, focus containment and an inert background.
- **When not to:** Use a non-modal dialog when the surrounding page must remain interactive.
- **Pitfall:** Setting `aria-modal="true"` on an ordinary element hides the rest of the page from assistive technology without making the page inert.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `dialog`). Chrome 37 / Firefox 98 / Safari 15.4.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Dialog (modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)

---

## 3. LIBRARY MAPPING

| Pattern | Integration boundary |
|---|---|
| Modal dialog | Close through the dialog lifecycle so focus returns to the opener. |
| Menu button | Use a disclosure and navigation list for site navigation; a menu role promises menu keyboard behavior. |
| Tabs, listbox or combobox | Do not add tabindex values or arrow-key handlers when a component manages roving focus; treat its autocomplete as a combobox and do not redeclare supplied roles. |
| Accordion, disclosure or tooltip | Keep expanded state aligned; disabled controls may not receive focus, and a tooltip cannot be the only label. |
| Status region, table or grid | Keep the live region mounted before changing its text; set `aria-sort` on the sorted header when needed. |
| Focus styling | Keep a visible replacement if an outline is removed. |

When a component library provides widget roles, state, focus movement or announcements, use that behavior as the source of truth. For hand-written widgets, implement the complete pattern described below.

---

## 4. NAMES AND FOCUS

### A2. Accessible name order

- **Rule:** Prefer `aria-labelledby` that points to visible text, and preserve the order `aria-labelledby`, `aria-label`, host-language label, then `title`.
- **Why:** A higher-priority naming source replaces lower-priority sources in the computed accessible name.
- **When not to:** Omit ARIA naming attributes when a native label already provides the intended name.
- **Pitfall:** An `aria-label` of `Send` replaces visible `Submit` text and can break speech input that uses the visible label.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: Accessible name calculation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Guides/Accessible_name_calculation)

### A3. Roving tabindex and active descendant

- **Rule:** Use roving tabindex for items that move DOM focus, and use `aria-activedescendant` when focus stays on a text input.
- **Why:** Roving tabindex moves browser focus, while `aria-activedescendant` exposes an active child without moving focus from its owner.
- **When not to:** Use neither pattern for ordinary links or buttons that already provide the needed keyboard behavior.
- **Pitfall:** The active descendant must reference a rendered element with a stable ID, so virtualized options can leave a dangling reference.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/)

### A4. Focus return through the dialog reference

- **Rule:** Close a library-managed overlay through its documented lifecycle so it can restore focus to the opener.
- **Why:** The component lifecycle can return focus after the modal leaves the top layer.
- **When not to:** Focus a logical successor when the opener no longer exists after the interaction.
- **Pitfall:** Removing a dialog through application state can bypass the component lifecycle and leave focus on `body`.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Dialog (modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)

### A5. Focus-visible styling

- **Rule:** Use `:focus-visible` for browser-selected focus styling and retain a clear keyboard focus indicator.
- **Why:** The browser tracks input modality and matches the selector when it determines a focus indicator is needed. Use [CS9](web-cascade-and-selectors.md#cs9-existing-state-selector-contract) for the state-selector contract that applies to focus styling.
- **When not to:** Add an explicit focus state when a programmatic focus change must always display a ring.
- **Pitfall:** Programmatic focus may not match `:focus-visible`, even when the newly focused container needs an indicator.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `focus-visible`). Chrome 86 / Firefox 85 / Safari 15.4.
- **See also:** [MDN: :focus-visible](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:focus-visible)

### A6. Inert background

- **Rule:** Set `inert` on the background while a custom modal is open, and leave the modal subtree interactive.
- **Why:** Inert removes descendants from sequential focus and interaction, while `aria-hidden` only changes the accessibility tree.
- **When not to:** Do not set `inert` when the surface is a non-modal overlay that leaves the page usable.
- **Pitfall:** Applying `inert` to the overlay itself makes its controls unreachable.
- **Support:** See [EA4](web-elements-and-attributes.md#ea4-inert-background-boundary) for browser support.
- **See also:** [MDN: inert global attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/inert)

---

## 5. ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PREFERENCES

### A7. Live-region timing

- **Rule:** Mount a live-region container before updating its text, set `aria-atomic="true"` when the whole message must be read and reserve assertive announcements for interrupting errors.
- **Why:** Assistive technology observes changes to an existing live region and may miss a region created with its first message.
- **When not to:** Do not add a live region to content already announced through ordinary navigation or focus movement.
- **Pitfall:** Recreating an alert region for each render can repeat the same message or fail to announce it.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: aria-live](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-live)

### A8. Forced colors

- **Rule:** Use system colors such as `Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `Highlight` and `HighlightText` for essential text, and use borders rather than shadows for boundaries in forced-colors mode.
- **Why:** The browser can replace author colors and remove background images when forced colors are active.
- **When not to:** Use `forced-color-adjust: none` only when preserving a specific color is necessary to convey meaning.
- **Pitfall:** Hard-coded SVG fills and shadow-only borders can disappear from the high-contrast presentation.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-03-12 (web-features `forced-colors`). Chrome 89 / Firefox 89 / Safari 16.
- **See also:** [MDN: forced-colors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors)

### A9. Reduced motion

- **Rule:** Put optional motion inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` and keep progress feedback available in both modes.
- **Why:** The default path remains safe when the preference is unknown or reduced, while the opt-in applies motion only to users who allow it.
- **When not to:** Do not add an animation when a state change is already clear without motion.
- **Pitfall:** A global animation reset can remove a loading spinner and leave no visible progress cue.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `prefers-reduced-motion`). Chrome 74 / Firefox 63 / Safari 10.1.
- **See also:** [MDN: prefers-reduced-motion](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion)

### A10. Contrast, color scheme and transparency preferences

- **Rule:** Set `color-scheme` for supported themes, honor contrast preferences, and treat reduced-transparency styling as a feature-detected enhancement over an opaque baseline.
- **Why:** The media preferences expose user display choices, while `color-scheme` lets browser controls adapt to the declared theme.
- **When not to:** Keep the opaque baseline when the interface has no transparency effect to reduce.
- **Pitfall:** Depending on `prefers-reduced-transparency` alone leaves Safari users without the fallback, and Firefox support requires a preference flag.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-11-30 (web-features `prefers-contrast`). Chrome 96 / Firefox 101 / Safari 14.1. Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `prefers-color-scheme`). Chrome 76 / Firefox 67 / Safari 12.1. Baseline widely available since 2024-08-03 (web-features `color-scheme`). Chrome 98 / Firefox 96 / Safari 13. Baseline limited availability (web-features `prefers-reduced-transparency`). Chrome 119 / Firefox unsupported / Safari unsupported.
- **See also:** [MDN: prefers-contrast](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-contrast)

---

## 6. WIDGET PATTERNS

### A11. Carousel

- **Rule:** Provide a visible rotation control, pause rotation on hover and focus and set `aria-live="off"` while it rotates.
- **Why:** Rotation changes content without user input, so a pause control and controlled announcements preserve predictable navigation.
- **When not to:** Omit rotation controls when the carousel never rotates automatically.
- **Pitfall:** Previous and next buttons without labels leave their direction unclear to screen-reader users.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Carousel](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/)

### A12. Table and grid

- **Rule:** Use a native table for static data and use `role="grid"` only when the widget implements its full keyboard interaction model.
- **Why:** A grid role promises managed focus and keyboard navigation beyond a table's row and column relationships.
- **When not to:** Use a grid when users edit, select or navigate cells as an interactive widget.
- **Pitfall:** A sortable table needs `aria-sort` on the currently sorted header.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Grid](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/)

### A13. Menu button

- **Rule:** Pair `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded` with Up or Down to open, Home and End, typeahead, Escape to close and return focus and Tab to close.
- **Why:** The menu-button pattern exposes a popup menu whose items use composite-widget keyboard behavior.
- **When not to:** Use a disclosure button and navigation list for site navigation.
- **Pitfall:** Applying `role="menu"` to ordinary site navigation changes assistive-technology expectations without supplying menu keyboard behavior.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Menu button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/)

### A14. Tooltip

- **Rule:** Give supplemental content `role="tooltip"`, associate its trigger through `aria-describedby`, show it on hover and focus and let Escape dismiss it.
- **Why:** The described-by relationship makes the tooltip's supplemental text available when the trigger receives focus.
- **When not to:** Use a dialog or popover when the content contains interactive controls.
- **Pitfall:** A tooltip on a disabled control may never appear, and a tooltip cannot provide the control's only name.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Tooltip](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/)

---

## 7. FORMS AND VALIDATION

### A15. Framework validation layers

- **Rule:** For forms handled by a framework validation layer, render app feedback and confirm whether the framework disables native browser validation. Keep native constraint attributes so the framework can read them.
- **Why:** A framework may add `novalidate` or otherwise replace browser validation bubbles while still using attributes such as `required` and `min` as validator inputs.
- **When not to:** Use browser-native validation when its message UI is the intended path.
- **Pitfall:** `setCustomValidity()` does not restore browser validation UI while `novalidate` remains on the form.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: Constraint validation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Constraint_validation)

### A16. Error association in library and hand-written fields

- **Rule:** Inside a component library's form-field wrapper, let the library associate its error and hint messages. In a hand-written field, bind the visible message ID and invalid state to the control.
- **Why:** A library may add message IDs to the input's `aria-describedby` list and update its `aria-invalid` state. For a hand-written field, give each message an ID, reference it from the control and set the invalid state when validation fails.
- **When not to:** Do not add a duplicate `aria-describedby` ID or invalid-state binding when the component already manages both.
- **Pitfall:** A library may show an error when a control is invalid and touched or when the form is submitted. A hand-written component that shows errors only when dirty behaves differently.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI: Forms tutorial, notifications](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/)

### A17. Error summary and focus on submit

- **Rule:** After a failed submit, focus the first invalid control or an error summary that links to each invalid control.
- **Why:** The summary gives assistive technology users one place to review errors and jump to the affected fields.
- **When not to:** A single-field form, such as a search box, can keep focus on its field and show the inline error there.
- **Pitfall:** After a submit handler marks every control as touched, focus remains on the submit button unless code moves it. Newly rendered error text is not automatically announced.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [WAI: Forms tutorial, notifications](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/)

### A18. Async validator pending state

- **Rule:** Block submission while a form is pending as well as when it is invalid. Expose validation progress with `aria-busy` on the field group or a polite status message.
- **Why:** An asynchronous validator can leave a form pending while both its valid and invalid states are false.
- **When not to:** A form with no async validators needs only the `invalid` check.
- **Pitfall:** A submit check that reads only `form.invalid` can run before async validation finishes. A disabled control leaves the tab order and is excluded from the form's aggregate value.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: Constraint validation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Constraint_validation)

---
title: Web Elements and Attributes
description: HTML element and attribute behavior for dialogs, popovers, forms, media hints and document language.
trigger_phrases:
  - "html dialog and popover behavior"
  - "form submission attributes"
  - "html resource loading attributes"
importance_tier: important
contextType: implementation
version: 1.0.1.0
---

# Web Elements and Attributes

HTML element and attribute behavior for dialogs, popovers, forms, media hints and document language.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

This file keeps the detailed HTML element and attribute mechanics.

### When to Use

- Adding a modal or non-modal overlay
- Building disclosure or inert content
- Wiring input and submission attributes
- Adding links, embeds or resource hints

### Boundaries

- Baseline web markup rules: [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
- Widget behavior, focus and the modal decision: [web-accessibility-patterns.md](web-accessibility-patterns.md).
- Inline language, bidirectional text and locale formatting: [web-internationalization.md](web-internationalization.md).

---

## 2. OVERLAYS

### EA1. Modal and non-modal dialog APIs

- **Rule:** Call `showModal()` for a modal `<dialog>`, and call `show()` only when the page must stay interactive. Treat `closedby` as an enhancement, feature-detect it and keep Escape plus an explicit close button available.
- **Why:** `showModal()` places the dialog in the top layer, creates a `::backdrop`, moves focus into the dialog and keeps sequential focus inside it. Escape dispatches a cancel request that closes the dialog unless the handler prevents it. `show()` does not make the rest of the page inert or establish modal focus behavior.
- **When not to:** Use `show()` for a non-modal prompt that leaves the surrounding page usable.
- **Pitfall:** Setting `aria-modal="true"` after calling `show()` does not create modal focus behavior.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `dialog`). Chrome 37 / Firefox 98 / Safari 15.4. Baseline limited availability (web-features `dialog-closedby`). Chrome 134 / Firefox 141 / Safari unsupported.
- **See also:** [MDN: dialog element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog)

### EA2. Popover states and invokers

- **Rule:** Use `popover="auto"` for light-dismiss behavior or `popover="manual"` when the project owns dismissal, and connect declarative controls with `popovertarget`. Feature-detect the `source` option and `popover="hint"`; keep an explicit anchor and an auto or manual popover path.
- **Why:** An auto popover joins the browser's auto popover stack and closes on light dismissal. A manual popover stays open until code or an explicit control closes it. `showPopover({ source })` can set the invoker as the implicit anchor for CSS anchor positioning.
- **When not to:** Use a dialog when the surface needs modal focus behavior or blocks the page behind it.
- **Pitfall:** `popover="hint"` can layer hint popovers without replacing an open auto popover, but its support is not uniform across the declared browsers.
- **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2025-01-27 (web-features `popover`). Chrome 116 / Firefox 125 / Safari 17. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome 137 / Firefox 144 / Safari 26. Baseline limited availability (web-features `popover-hint`). Chrome 151 / Firefox 153 / Safari unsupported.
- **See also:** [MDN: Using the Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API/Using)

---

## 3. DISCLOSURE AND INERT CONTENT

### EA3. Exclusive details and find-in-page content

- **Rule:** Use `<summary>` as the first child of `<details>`, and share a `name` only when one-open-at-a-time disclosure is intended.
- **Why:** The summary is the disclosure's activation control, and details elements with the same name form an exclusive group. When `hidden="until-found"` is supported, listen for `beforematch` to reveal a containing disclosure before the browser scrolls to a match. Keep an explicit reveal control as the baseline.
- **When not to:** Leave details elements unnamed when readers need to compare several open sections.
- **Pitfall:** Removing or collapsing a hidden ancestor after `beforematch` can hide the found text again before the browser scrolls to it. The `beforematch` compatibility row is unconfirmed, so keep an explicit reveal control.
- **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-09-03 (web-features `details-name`). Chrome 120 / Firefox 130 / Safari 17.2. Baseline limited availability (web-features `hidden-until-found`). Chrome 102 / Firefox 148 / Safari unsupported.
- **See also:** [MDN: hidden global attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/hidden)

### EA4. Inert background boundary

- **Rule:** Set `inert` only on the background subtree that must stop receiving focus and interaction while a custom modal is open.
- **Why:** The attribute makes descendant controls unavailable for focus and user interaction until it is removed. See [A6](web-accessibility-patterns.md#a6-inert-background) for the modal decision about when the background needs this boundary.
- **When not to:** Do not inert the background for a non-modal surface that leaves page controls usable.
- **Pitfall:** If the overlay sits inside the subtree marked `inert`, its own controls become unavailable too.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-10-11 (web-features `inert`). Chrome 102 / Firefox 112 / Safari 15.5.
- **See also:** [MDN: inert global attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/inert)

---

## 4. INPUT AND SUBMISSION ATTRIBUTES

### EA5. Keyboard hints and autocomplete tokens

- **Rule:** Set `inputmode` for the expected data, `enterkeyhint` for the next action and `autocomplete` for the field's actual purpose.
- **Why:** Keyboard hints influence the virtual keyboard without validating the value. Autocomplete tokens let browsers and credential managers identify fields by meaning. Use `username`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `one-time-code` and `webauthn` for sign-in, password, verification and passkey flows. Use `cc-name`, `cc-given-name`, `cc-additional-name`, `cc-family-name`, `cc-number`, `cc-exp`, `cc-exp-month`, `cc-exp-year`, `cc-csc` and `cc-type` for payment-card fields. Use `tel-national` for a national phone number and `address-line1`, `address-line2` or `address-line3` for separate address lines.
- **When not to:** Omit a keyboard hint when the default keyboard already fits the input and its next action.
- **Pitfall:** Using `autocomplete="off"` on sign-in or payment fields can block useful credential or payment autofill.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-06-07 (web-features `inputmode`). Chrome 66 / Firefox 95 / Safari 12.1. Baseline widely available since 2024-05-02 (web-features `enterkeyhint`). Chrome 77 / Firefox 94 / Safari 13.1. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome Unknown / Firefox Unknown / Safari Unknown.
- **See also:** [MDN: autocomplete attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/autocomplete)

### EA6. Form owner and submitter overrides

- **Rule:** Set `form` when a control belongs to a form elsewhere in the document, and read the activated submitter's override when handling submission.
- **Why:** A control's `form` attribute associates it with a form by ID. The submitter's `formaction` overrides the owning form's `action` for that submission.
- **When not to:** Omit these attributes when every control is inside its form and all submitters share one destination.
- **Pitfall:** Reading only `form.action` ignores a submit button's `formaction` destination.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [HTML spec: Form submission algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#form-submission-algorithm)

---

## 5. LINKS, EMBEDS AND RESOURCE HINTS

### EA7. Link isolation and request credentials

- **Rule:** Add `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to a new-tab link when it must not control the opener, and choose `referrerpolicy` and `crossorigin` for the request's privacy and CORS needs. Common referrer policy values include `no-referrer`, `origin` and `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.
- **Why:** `noopener` removes the new browsing context's access to its opener. `noreferrer` also suppresses the referrer. `crossorigin` selects how a media request uses CORS credentials.
- **When not to:** Keep the referrer when the destination depends on it for a documented analytics or return-flow contract.
- **Pitfall:** Adding `noreferrer` without checking the destination can remove attribution that the product expects.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-03-20 (web-features `referrer-policy`). Chrome 85 / Firefox 87 / Safari 15. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome 13 / Firefox 8 / Safari 6.
- **See also:** [MDN: rel=noopener](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/noopener)

### EA8. Image loading and decoding hints

- **Rule:** Treat `fetchpriority` as a scheduler hint, `loading` as a fetch timing hint and `decoding` as a display scheduling hint.
- **Why:** These attributes affect different stages of image work and do not replace reserved dimensions or correct source selection.
- **When not to:** Leave default priority on ordinary images that are neither urgent nor a known loading bottleneck.
- **Pitfall:** Lazy-loading an image that becomes the largest contentful paint delays the page's primary visual response. See the [LCP resource rule](web-performance-and-loading.md#p1-largest-contentful-paint-resource).
- **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-10-29 (web-features `fetch-priority`). Chrome 103 / Firefox 132 / Safari 17.2. Baseline widely available since 2026-06-19 (web-features `loading-lazy`). Chrome 77 / Firefox 121 / Safari 16.4. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome 65 / Firefox 63 / Safari 11.1.
- **See also:** [MDN: img element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/img)

### EA9. Document language and translation hints

- **Rule:** Keep `lang`, `dir` and `translate` aligned with the language and direction of the content.
- **Why:** These attributes expose language and text direction to browser features and assistive technology, while `translate="no"` marks names or code that machine translation should retain. Inline language, bidirectional text and locale formatting details are in [web-internationalization.md](web-internationalization.md#2-language-and-direction).
- **When not to:** Do not set a local language or direction override when the text follows the surrounding passage.
- **Pitfall:** A missing inline language or direction override can make a short foreign phrase render or sound incorrectly inside otherwise correct page metadata.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2018-01-29 (web-features `lang-attr`). Chrome 1 / Firefox 1 / Safari ≤4. Baseline widely available since 2018-01-29 (web-features `dir`). Chrome 1 / Firefox 1 / Safari 3. Baseline widely available since 2025-09-14 (web-features `translate`). Chrome 19 / Firefox 111 / Safari 6.
- **See also:** [MDN: lang global attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/lang)

---

## 6. SUPPORT

Support summaries show each feature's web-features Baseline classification and browser versions.

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari | Baseline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Dialog | 37 | 98 | 15.4 | widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `dialog`) |
| `closedby` | 134 | 141 | unsupported | limited availability (web-features `dialog-closedby`) |
| Popover auto/manual | 116 | 125 | 17 | newly available since 2025-01-27 (web-features `popover`) |
| Popover source option | 137 | 144 | 26 | Baseline: no web-features entry. |
| Popover hint | 151 | 153 | unsupported | limited availability (web-features `popover-hint`) |
