# Web Elements and Attributes

HTML element and attribute behavior for dialogs, popovers, forms, media hints and document language.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

This file keeps the detailed HTML element and attribute mechanics.

### When to Use

- Adding a modal or non-modal overlay
- Building disclosure or inert content
- Wiring input and submission attributes
- Adding links, embeds or resource hints

### Boundaries

- Baseline web markup rules: [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
- Widget behavior, focus and the modal decision: [web-accessibility-patterns.md](web-accessibility-patterns.md).
- Inline language, bidirectional text and locale formatting: [web-internationalization.md](web-internationalization.md).

---

## 2. OVERLAYS

### EA1. Modal and non-modal dialog APIs

- **Rule:** Call `showModal()` for a modal `<dialog>`, and call `show()` only when the page must stay interactive. Treat `closedby` as an enhancement, feature-detect it and keep Escape plus an explicit close button available.
- **Why:** `showModal()` places the dialog in the top layer, creates a `::backdrop`, moves focus into the dialog and keeps sequential focus inside it. Escape dispatches a cancel request that closes the dialog unless the handler prevents it. `show()` does not make the rest of the page inert or establish modal focus behavior.
- **When not to:** Use `show()` for a non-modal prompt that leaves the surrounding page usable.
- **Pitfall:** Setting `aria-modal="true"` after calling `show()` does not create modal focus behavior.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `dialog`). Chrome 37 / Firefox 98 / Safari 15.4. Baseline limited availability (web-features `dialog-closedby`). Chrome 134 / Firefox 141 / Safari unsupported.
- **See also:** [MDN: dialog element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog)

### EA2. Popover states and invokers

- **Rule:** Use `popover="auto"` for light-dismiss behavior or `popover="manual"` when the project owns dismissal, and connect declarative controls with `popovertarget`. Feature-detect the `source` option and `popover="hint"`; keep an explicit anchor and an auto or manual popover path.
- **Why:** An auto popover joins the browser's auto popover stack and closes on light dismissal. A manual popover stays open until code or an explicit control closes it. `showPopover({ source })` can set the invoker as the implicit anchor for CSS anchor positioning.
- **When not to:** Use a dialog when the surface needs modal focus behavior or blocks the page behind it.
- **Pitfall:** `popover="hint"` can layer hint popovers without replacing an open auto popover, but its support is not uniform across the declared browsers.
- **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2025-01-27 (web-features `popover`). Chrome 116 / Firefox 125 / Safari 17. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome 137 / Firefox 144 / Safari 26. Baseline limited availability (web-features `popover-hint`). Chrome 151 / Firefox 153 / Safari unsupported.
- **See also:** [MDN: Using the Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API/Using)

---

## 3. DISCLOSURE AND INERT CONTENT

### EA3. Exclusive details and find-in-page content

- **Rule:** Use `<summary>` as the first child of `<details>`, and share a `name` only when one-open-at-a-time disclosure is intended.
- **Why:** The summary is the disclosure's activation control, and details elements with the same name form an exclusive group. When `hidden="until-found"` is supported, listen for `beforematch` to reveal a containing disclosure before the browser scrolls to a match. Keep an explicit reveal control as the baseline.
- **When not to:** Leave details elements unnamed when readers need to compare several open sections.
- **Pitfall:** Removing or collapsing a hidden ancestor after `beforematch` can hide the found text again before the browser scrolls to it. The `beforematch` compatibility row is unconfirmed, so keep an explicit reveal control.
- **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-09-03 (web-features `details-name`). Chrome 120 / Firefox 130 / Safari 17.2. Baseline limited availability (web-features `hidden-until-found`). Chrome 102 / Firefox 148 / Safari unsupported.
- **See also:** [MDN: hidden global attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/hidden)

### EA4. Inert background boundary

- **Rule:** Set `inert` only on the background subtree that must stop receiving focus and interaction while a custom modal is open.
- **Why:** The attribute makes descendant controls unavailable for focus and user interaction until it is removed. See [A6](web-accessibility-patterns.md#a6-inert-background) for the modal decision about when the background needs this boundary.
- **When not to:** Do not inert the background for a non-modal surface that leaves page controls usable.
- **Pitfall:** If the overlay sits inside the subtree marked `inert`, its own controls become unavailable too.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-10-11 (web-features `inert`). Chrome 102 / Firefox 112 / Safari 15.5.
- **See also:** [MDN: inert global attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/inert)

---

## 4. INPUT AND SUBMISSION ATTRIBUTES

### EA5. Keyboard hints and autocomplete tokens

- **Rule:** Set `inputmode` for the expected data, `enterkeyhint` for the next action and `autocomplete` for the field's actual purpose.
- **Why:** Keyboard hints influence the virtual keyboard without validating the value. Autocomplete tokens let browsers and credential managers identify fields by meaning. Use `username`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `one-time-code` and `webauthn` for sign-in, password, verification and passkey flows. Use `cc-name`, `cc-given-name`, `cc-additional-name`, `cc-family-name`, `cc-number`, `cc-exp`, `cc-exp-month`, `cc-exp-year`, `cc-csc` and `cc-type` for payment-card fields. Use `tel-national` for a national phone number and `address-line1`, `address-line2` or `address-line3` for separate address lines.
- **When not to:** Omit a keyboard hint when the default keyboard already fits the input and its next action.
- **Pitfall:** Using `autocomplete="off"` on sign-in or payment fields can block useful credential or payment autofill.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-06-07 (web-features `inputmode`). Chrome 66 / Firefox 95 / Safari 12.1. Baseline widely available since 2024-05-02 (web-features `enterkeyhint`). Chrome 77 / Firefox 94 / Safari 13.1. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome Unknown / Firefox Unknown / Safari Unknown.
- **See also:** [MDN: autocomplete attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/autocomplete)

### EA6. Form owner and submitter overrides

- **Rule:** Set `form` when a control belongs to a form elsewhere in the document, and read the activated submitter's override when handling submission.
- **Why:** A control's `form` attribute associates it with a form by ID. The submitter's `formaction` overrides the owning form's `action` for that submission.
- **When not to:** Omit these attributes when every control is inside its form and all submitters share one destination.
- **Pitfall:** Reading only `form.action` ignores a submit button's `formaction` destination.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [HTML spec: Form submission algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#form-submission-algorithm)

---

## 5. LINKS, EMBEDS AND RESOURCE HINTS

### EA7. Link isolation and request credentials

- **Rule:** Add `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to a new-tab link when it must not control the opener, and choose `referrerpolicy` and `crossorigin` for the request's privacy and CORS needs. Common referrer policy values include `no-referrer`, `origin` and `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.
- **Why:** `noopener` removes the new browsing context's access to its opener. `noreferrer` also suppresses the referrer. `crossorigin` selects how a media request uses CORS credentials.
- **When not to:** Keep the referrer when the destination depends on it for a documented analytics or return-flow contract.
- **Pitfall:** Adding `noreferrer` without checking the destination can remove attribution that the product expects.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-03-20 (web-features `referrer-policy`). Chrome 85 / Firefox 87 / Safari 15. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome 13 / Firefox 8 / Safari 6.
- **See also:** [MDN: rel=noopener](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/noopener)

### EA8. Image loading and decoding hints

- **Rule:** Treat `fetchpriority` as a scheduler hint, `loading` as a fetch timing hint and `decoding` as a display scheduling hint.
- **Why:** These attributes affect different stages of image work and do not replace reserved dimensions or correct source selection.
- **When not to:** Leave default priority on ordinary images that are neither urgent nor a known loading bottleneck.
- **Pitfall:** Lazy-loading an image that becomes the largest contentful paint delays the page's primary visual response. See the [LCP resource rule](web-performance-and-loading.md#p1-largest-contentful-paint-resource).
- **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-10-29 (web-features `fetch-priority`). Chrome 103 / Firefox 132 / Safari 17.2. Baseline widely available since 2026-06-19 (web-features `loading-lazy`). Chrome 77 / Firefox 121 / Safari 16.4. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome 65 / Firefox 63 / Safari 11.1.
- **See also:** [MDN: img element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/img)

### EA9. Document language and translation hints

- **Rule:** Keep `lang`, `dir` and `translate` aligned with the language and direction of the content.
- **Why:** These attributes expose language and text direction to browser features and assistive technology, while `translate="no"` marks names or code that machine translation should retain. Inline language, bidirectional text and locale formatting details are in [web-internationalization.md](web-internationalization.md#2-language-and-direction).
- **When not to:** Do not set a local language or direction override when the text follows the surrounding passage.
- **Pitfall:** A missing inline language or direction override can make a short foreign phrase render or sound incorrectly inside otherwise correct page metadata.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2018-01-29 (web-features `lang-attr`). Chrome 1 / Firefox 1 / Safari ≤4. Baseline widely available since 2018-01-29 (web-features `dir`). Chrome 1 / Firefox 1 / Safari 3. Baseline widely available since 2025-09-14 (web-features `translate`). Chrome 19 / Firefox 111 / Safari 6.

# Web Internationalization

HTML language and direction, bidirectional text, locale formatting and translation-tolerant layout.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

This file keeps browser language, direction and locale formatting mechanics. Support summaries use the web-features Baseline classifications and browser-version data.

### When to Use

- Setting language tags or text direction
- Isolating bidirectional text
- Following the writing mode or mirroring directional icons
- Formatting dates, numbers and plurals by locale
- Testing layouts for translated text growth

### Boundaries

- Baseline web markup rules: [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
- Logical property mechanics and writing modes: [web-layout-and-sizing.md](web-layout-and-sizing.md).
- Element and attribute mechanics for `lang`, `dir` and `translate`: [web-elements-and-attributes.md](web-elements-and-attributes.md).

---

## 2. LANGUAGE AND DIRECTION

### I1. Language tags

- **Rule:** Set a valid BCP 47 `lang` on the document and on inline spans whose language differs from the surrounding text.
- **Why:** Browsers and assistive technology use language metadata for pronunciation, hyphenation, spellcheck and language-aware selectors.
- **When not to:** Omit a local override when the phrase uses the surrounding language.
- **Pitfall:** A correct document language does not identify a foreign-language name or phrase inside an otherwise different-language paragraph.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2018-01-29 (web-features `lang-attr`). Chrome 1 / Firefox 1 / Safari ≤4.
- **See also:** [MDN: lang global attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/lang)

### I2. Direction and automatic direction

- **Rule:** Set `dir="rtl"` for a right-to-left document and use `dir="auto"` for user-provided strings with unknown direction.
- **Why:** Automatic direction follows the first strong directional character, while an explicit document direction controls the page's base writing direction.
- **When not to:** Keep the inherited direction when a string is known to follow the surrounding content.
- **Pitfall:** Under `dir="auto"`, an Arabic username that begins with a Latin brand name is treated as left-to-right, because the first strong character decides. Digits are weak and do not decide.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2018-01-29 (web-features `dir`). Chrome 1 / Firefox 1 / Safari 3.
- **See also:** [MDN: dir global attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/dir)

### I3. Bidirectional isolation

- **Rule:** Wrap interpolated user text in `<bdi>` or isolate an inline span with `unicode-bidi: isolate`.
- **Why:** Isolation keeps the embedded text's directional ordering from affecting adjacent text and punctuation.
- **When not to:** Skip an isolate when the embedded text is already in a separate block with its own direction.
- **Pitfall:** An RTL name interpolated into an LTR sentence can move the trailing punctuation to the wrong visual side.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `bdi`). Chrome 16 / Firefox 10 / Safari 6.
- **See also:** [MDN: bdi element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/bdi)

---

## 3. LAYOUT AND DIRECTIONAL ICONS

### I4. Logical properties and writing modes

- **Rule:** Use the CSS mapping in [web-layout-and-sizing.md](web-layout-and-sizing.md#6-logical-properties) when dimensions and edges must follow the writing mode.
- **Why:** The layout reference owns the physical-to-logical property mechanics and their interaction with writing modes.
- **When not to:** Keep physical coordinates for intentionally physical surfaces such as a canvas whose origin is fixed to the left edge.
- **Pitfall:** Mixing physical and logical sides in one rule lets declaration order choose the edge in one direction and a different edge in another.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS logical properties and values](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_logical_properties_and_values)

### I5. Directional icon mirroring

- **Rule:** Mirror arrows and chevrons whose meaning follows inline reading direction, and keep direction-neutral or physical icons unchanged.
- **Why:** Directional icons encode forward or backward movement, while a logo, clock, checkmark or media control keeps the same meaning in either writing direction.
- **When not to:** Do not mirror an icon whose symbol depicts a fixed physical object or an invariant action.
- **Pitfall:** Mirroring a play or checkmark icon reverses a symbol whose meaning does not depend on text direction.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [W3C International: Script direction and languages](https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-scripts)

---

## 4. LOCALE FORMATTING

### I6. Intl formatting and plural categories

- **Rule:** Pass the active locale explicitly to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `NumberFormat`, `PluralRules`, `RelativeTimeFormat`, `ListFormat`, `Collator`, `Segmenter` and `DisplayNames`.
- **Why:** An explicit locale keeps formatting aligned with the app language instead of the browser's unrelated default. `PluralRules` exposes locale-specific categories, including six categories in Arabic and few or many categories in Polish.
- **When not to:** Use a locale-independent representation when the value is an identifier or machine protocol field rather than reader-facing text.
- **Pitfall:** A `count === 1` branch assumes two plural forms and fails for languages with additional categories.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: Intl](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl)

### I7. Date-only parsing

- **Rule:** Parse date-only values as calendar dates in the intended locale and time zone instead of converting them through UTC timestamps.
- **Why:** JavaScript parses an ISO date-only string such as `2026-11-02` at UTC midnight, which can display as the previous local date in a negative offset.
- **When not to:** Use a timestamp when the input represents an exact instant rather than a calendar date.
- **Pitfall:** Calling `toISOString().slice(0, 10)` on a local date can serialize a different calendar day.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: Date.parse()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Date/parse)

---

## 5. TRANSLATION-TOLERANT TEXT

### I9. Expansion and pseudo-localization

- **Rule:** Test layouts with pseudo-localized text and leave room for German and Dutch strings that can grow by about 30 to 35 percent.
- **Why:** Translation changes word length and line breaks, which can push fixed-width controls past their available space.
- **When not to:** Use a fixed measure only when the content has a documented hard limit, such as a machine identifier.
- **Pitfall:** A button that fits the source language can clip its translated label when its width is fixed.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: Localization and plurals](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Localization/Localization_and_Plurals)

label_new = re.compile(r'^- \*\*(Rule|Why|When not to|Pitfall|Support|See also):\*\* (.*)$')
label_old = re.compile(r'^\*\*(Rule|Why|When not to|Pitfall|Support|See also)\.\*\* (.*)$')

def items(text):
    out=[]
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = label_new.match(line) or label_old.match(line)
        if m:
            out.append((m.group(1), m.group(2)))
    return out

        c = ci[i] if i < len(ci) else None
        if h != c:
            mism+=1
            print(f"  [{i}] HEAD {h}\n       CUR  {c}")

import re, subprocess

files = [
 ".skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-frontend/references/web-accessibility-patterns.md",
 ".skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-frontend/references/web-elements-and-attributes.md",

]

label_new = re.compile(r'^- \*\*(Rule|Why|When not to|Pitfall|Support|See also):\*\* (.*)$')
label_old = re.compile(r'^\*\*(Rule|Why|When not to|Pitfall|Support|See also)\.\*\* (.*)$')

def items(text):
    out=[]
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = label_new.match(line) or label_old.match(line)
        if m:
            out.append((m.group(1), m.group(2)))
    return out

for f in files:
    head = subprocess.run(["git","show",f"HEAD:{f}"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
    cur = open(f).read()
    hi, ci = items(head), items(cur)
    print(f"== {f}\nHEAD items {len(hi)}  CURRENT items {len(ci)}")
    # pair by index, report body mismatches
    n=max(len(hi),len(ci))
    mism=0
    for i in range(n):
        h = hi[i] if i < len(hi) else None
        c = ci[i] if i < len(ci) else None
        if h != c:
            mism+=1
            print(f"  [{i}] HEAD {h}\n       CUR  {c}")
    print(f"  mismatches: {mism}")

"""Check every relative Markdown link that targets a sk-code-frontend reference resolves to a file and heading."""
import re, sys, pathlib, subprocess
root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
ref_dir = root / ".skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-frontend/references"
def slug(h):
    s = h.strip().lower()
    s = re.sub(r'[^\w\- ]', '', s)
    return s.replace(' ', '-')
def anchors(p):
    out, fence = set(), False
    for line in p.read_text().split('\n'):
        if line.startswith('```'): fence = not fence
        if fence: continue
        m = re.match(r'^#{1,6} (.+)$', line)
        if m: out.add(slug(re.sub(r'[`*]', '', m.group(1))))
    return out
files = subprocess.run(['git','ls-files','*.md'], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
bad = checked = 0
link = re.compile(r'\]\(([^)\s]+?)\)')
for f in files:
    if f.startswith('specs/') or '/z_archive/' in f or f.startswith('.hermes/'): continue
    src = root / f
    if not src.is_file(): continue
    for n, line in enumerate(src.read_text(errors='ignore').split('\n'), 1):
        for target in link.findall(line):
            if target.startswith(('http', 'mailto:')): continue
            path, _, frag = target.partition('#')
            tp = (src.parent / path).resolve() if path else src.resolve()
            if not (str(tp).startswith(str(ref_dir)) or (not path and str(src.resolve()).startswith(str(ref_dir)))): continue
            checked += 1
            if not tp.exists():
                print(f"MISSING FILE {f}:{n} -> {target}"); bad += 1; continue
            if frag and tp.suffix == '.md' and frag not in anchors(tp):
                print(f"MISSING ANCHOR {f}:{n} -> {target}"); bad += 1
print(f"checked={checked} broken={bad}")
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

LABELS = ["Rule","Why","When not to","Pitfall","Support","See also"]
pat = re.compile(r'^\*\*(' + '|'.join(map(re.escape,LABELS)) + r')\.\*\* ?(.*)$')
def transform(text):
    out=[]
    for line in text.split('\n'):
        m=pat.match(line)
        if m:
            label,body=m.group(1),m.group(2)
            if label=="Support" and out and out[-1].startswith("- **Support:** "):
                out[-1]=out[-1].rstrip()+" "+body; continue
            out.append(f"- **{label}:** {body}"); continue
        if line=='---' and out and out[-1].strip()!='' and len(out)>12: out.append('')
        out.append(line)
    return '\n'.join(out)

for f in files:
    head=subprocess.run(["git","show",f"HEAD:{f}"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
    pre=[l for l in transform(head).split('\n') if l.startswith('### ')]
    cur=open(f).read().split('\n')
    curh=[l for l in cur if l.startswith('### ')]
    removed=[h for h in pre if h not in curh]
    added=[h for h in curh if h not in pre]
    print(f"== {f}\n  removed: {removed}\n  added:   {added}")
    # separator padding check
    bad=[]
    for i,l in enumerate(cur):
        if l.strip()=='---' and i>12:
            before = cur[i-1] if i>0 else ''
            after = cur[i+1] if i+1<len(cur) else ''
            if before.strip()!='' or after.strip()!='':
                bad.append((i+1,repr(before),repr(after)))
    print(f"  unpadded separators: {bad if bad else 'none'}")
